entries.tip: Never withhold a useful result to bait a counterclaim. Investigators: once you hold a result that bears on a vote, post the target and exact result, with as much of your role as the result needs to be believed and checked, in your first speech after getting it, or the moment someone asks, and keep your last will current. Naming your exact role feeds a possible Ritualist, whose guess kills through any Medic (t55): when one may be in the game, put the full log in your will before you claim and expect to die that night. A result held back and revealed after an opponent's claim looks retrofitted, above all when it names the player who just accused you. A hidden investigator who votes with the Yakuza looks exactly like a fake. Exception: with no result yet, or only a weak one, don't name your exact role on Day 2, and never say you will act or spend a token tonight. A firm exact claim of a role off the Roleplayer list (Bloodhound, Juror, Scrutineer...) is a sure Ritualist kill, so wait until the claim changes a vote. If someone else claims your role or exact result, say so at once, in your next message, with your full log. Only Smuggler and Vulture are Unique, so a second claimant of any other role may be as real as you: state your claim and ask them for something checkable (tokens, results), but don't call them a liar on the clash alone, and never fire a kill token at them over it (t313). Being second after a vague opener reads as copying, so ask the rival for the exact wording of their private result before you post yours. Never vote against your own information to 'wait and see'. If you must vote in a way that looks odd, explain why during that trial.

entries.tip: When two Sheriff claimants call each other Evil, both results can be true: Executioners and Jesters read Evil. An early Day 2 Evil claim against someone who fights hard to survive may be an Executioner push. Don't hang on who sounded better: look for a mechanical check (which claimant the Katana attacks, a Medic's stated protect that matches a survival, a death that contradicts a read). Waiting a Day for one is cheap only on a large table with a single killer. If the night's causes of death show two killers (Katana plus a Serial Killer) or few players are left, a no-hang Day can lose the game: ask both claimants for night, target and exact result, then hang that Day from the duel or the unclaimed pool (t101).

entries.tip: Assume the real holder of any role you fake-claim is alive and will counterclaim, that an Accountant can audit your exact token count, that an exact-role check (Oracle, Ritualist, Diviner, Archivist, Surveyor or Profiler list) can rule your claimed role out, and that a public role list plus self-proving effects (prosecutions, cleans, ignites) and confirmed claims can leave no slot for it. Never claim a Unique role whose holder may be alive. Never copy a role whose actions were already public (e.g. a Prosecutor): the real holder will counterclaim with earlier reads and correct night labels. Never claim the role that a dead victim you visited had claimed in public or in their will. Pick a fake role whose tokens match yours: claim a tokenless role only if you hold no tokens. Never volunteer your token history or report more results than the role's tokens allow. Visit results include Lookout and Tracker logs, Insomniac role lists, Scout and Cartographer groups and FT counts. Before any claim that includes a visit, check it against every visit result already posted: a claimed track or watch that an existing count rules out (e.g. a 'track' on a night an Insomniac saw exactly one visitor, a confirmed Lookout) is exposed within a round. A no-action claim is unsafe if you visited a target someone may have watched, so prepare a story that fits a token check or visit report. If you fake a visiting role (Tracker, Lookout), name your real visit destinations as your targets so these results can only confirm you, and fix the claim in night chat before you need it. Never improvise targets. If your claim is broken, don't switch to another claim: a withdrawn claim plus a fallback (above all a crowded Vanilla) is a mechanical case on its own.

entries.tip: Dying with unused tokens is the usual Vigilante failure: holding all your shots makes you a Vanilla Villager. Shoot on a lead, not on proof. Set a concrete trigger by Day 2-3 and fire a Basic shot (1 token) once it's met, and fire anyway by the time the Yakuza could be near parity. Good leads include a claim conflict, an Evil check against an unverifiable claim, a credible map or group result that leaves one unconfirmed member as the likely holder, or the stated votes and PM partners of a player shown Yakuza by a mechanical result (e.g. those who said they voted No on that player's nomination, argued to delay the hang, or whose stated votes the totals contradict). Roles are hidden on death and hard leads are scarce, so the strongest claimless voice is a fair target: someone who leads nominations on 'silence' or always echoes the consensus without results. A lone read/vote mismatch or one player's private request is not enough on its own; bring a PM'd request into public first. Traits (R24) raise the cost of a wrong shot, and no investigation sees them: killing a Cursed villager also Divine-attacks a random Good player, and killing an Avenger kills you too. A Basic shot that fails on a suspect no credible Medic protects is evidence of innate Defense (Arsonist or Serial Killer Standard, Jester or Executioner Basic), so post it the next Day. If you already suspect a Neutral killer and want the kill, only a Strong shot (3 tokens) beats Standard Defense. If your shot kills, you learn the victim's role. That is one of the few ways a dead player's role becomes known, so post the night, target and role the next Day. Claim only once your shots have paid off: the claim names your exact role to a possible Ritualist, whose guess no Medic stops, so expect to die that night and fire any shot you still have a lead for.

Good leads include a claim conflict, an Evil check against an unverifiable claim, a credible map or group result that leaves one unconfirmed member as the likely holder, or the stated votes and PM partners of a player shown Yakuza by a mechanical result (e.g. those who said they voted No on that player's nomination, argued to delay the hang, or whose stated votes the totals contradict). Roles are hidden on death and hard leads are scarce, so the strongest claimless voice is a fair target: someone who leads nominations on 'silence' or always echoes the consensus without results. A lone read/vote mismatch or one player's private request is not enough on its own; bring a PM'd request into public first. If you hit a hidden Cardinal, the curse Divine-attacks a random Good player. A Basic shot that fails on a suspect no credible Medic protects is evidence of innate Defense (Arsonist or Serial Killer Standard, Jester or Executioner Basic), so post it the next Day. If you already suspect a Neutral killer and want the kill, only a Strong shot (3 tokens) beats Standard Defense. If your shot kills, you learn the victim's role. That is one of the few ways a dead player's role becomes known, so post the night, target and role the next Day. Claim only once your shots have paid off.
history.note: Revision, not a game: added the Ritualist cost to the advice to post a kill report and claim.

entries.tip: Protect the likeliest Katana targets: vocal analysts early, then claimed investigators. Never protect a claimed or likely Veteran who may still hold alert tokens: your protection is a visit, an alert Strong-attacks every visitor (your own Standard Defense wouldn't stop it), and a Veteran on alert already has Standard Defense (t153). Guard another likely target instead. Free Standard protection, used night after night, can carry the town, but it stops only Basic and Standard attacks such as the Katana. A Serial Killer's attack and an Arsonist's ignite are Strong and go straight through it. Once a cause of death, an archive or a profile points to a Neutral killer, or the Katana has gone quiet because the Yakuza look dead, spend a token on Strong protection (1 token on another player) for your most valuable ally on each night a Strong kill is likely; an ignite hits every doused player at once. While the Katana still kills, the night after you publicly claim Medic you are the likeliest target, so spend a token on Standard self-protection that night. If a Serial Killer cause of death has already appeared, Standard self-protection won't stop its Strong attack: Strong self-protection costs both tokens and leaves your ward unguarded, so the real answer is to stay unclaimed and never say you will protect tonight (t94). After you save a claimed investigator, the Yakuza will either retry them or switch to you. Keep free protection on them on most nights, but while your claim is public and you still hold tokens, spend one within the next night or two rather than dying with both. Strong doesn't stop a Divine guess. Don't follow a fixed pattern a Pharmacist or holder can predict. Dying, or ending the game, with unspent tokens wastes them.

entries.tip: A visit shows a destination, not an action or alignment. A track or watch cannot tell protection from framing or a Katana attack. A Lookout sees only visitors to their target, so watching the Katana holder shows nothing about the holder's attack. Killing an attacker at night does not cancel their attack that same night. A Lookout never sees their own visit, but that only matters if the Lookout could be the holder. If the reporter has independent support (a Tracker confirms their visits, earlier reports checked out, the named visitors confirm themselves) and X is the only other visitor to a Katana victim, treat it as near-proof against X. The same applies when several visitors are named and all but X have confirmed harmless explanations: X is then the lone unexplained visitor. This holds even more when X first denied the visit, claims a role that doesn't fit, or was the sole visitor to victims on several nights. Don't let 'a visit isn't an attack' or the self-visit caveat acquit such a visitor. 'Corroborated' is the condition that matters. A lone-visitor report (watch, track or map) from one unverified claimant with no second source is only that claimant's word, and a Jester or Yakuza can invent exactly this pattern, 'denied visit' included. Give it no weight if it was held back, names the claimant's own accuser, or is contradicted by claimants who confirm each other (t296).

entries.tip: Keep hostile Neutrals (SK, Arsonist) in the suspect pool all game, not only after the Yakuza die. Once an archive, survey or kill pattern suggests one exists, give every player a slot and keep a running list of candidates. Press anyone who admits a night action ('I took an action elsewhere') but won't name a role or target: treat it as a douse until explained. Press the quiet unclaimed players who give only measured, non-committal comments, and ask each for a claim. An Arsonist kills no one until it ignites, so quiet nights don't mean it's harmless; expect a multi-death night. A Not Evil Sheriff result or a Vanilla claim doesn't clear them. A failed attack with no block notice can mean innate Defense, not just a Medic. Doused Yakuza and Neutrals are told an Arsonist doused them, but Good players never are. A player who says they were doused has therefore admitted they aren't Good.

entries.tip: Don't defend a doomed teammate. Ballots are secret, but the totals are announced, and the town compares them with what everyone said. entries.tip: On the first Day (Day 2), don't hint at a protective role, an info role, a Veteran or your tokens. A half-hint ('my role reads past trials') is the worst of both: it draws a Day of pressure, forces the full claim anyway and marks you for the night kill. Either give no hint at all, or once you are pressed past one calm non-answer, claim plainly once rather than dodging for rounds (t188). If someone else drops a hint, don't ask them about it in public; that spreads the hint. A flat, repeated refusal to claim is itself a hint: answer claim requests with a quiet, cooperative non-answer instead of making the refusal the day's topic. Investigators should still post results publicly once they matter, not only in a will that may come too late; a Night 1 result that bears on Day 2 already matters. When a Ritualist may be alive, never name another living player's exact role in your will or in public; write 'one of X/Y holds info, ask them'. The same care applies to your own role: a firm Day 2 claim of a role off the Roleplayer list, made with no result or a weak one, is a free Ritualist kill (t55).

entries.tip: Never speak publicly from your hidden perspective. Say 'died to a Katana', never 'my Katana'. Never state as fact anything you know only from night chat or the Yakuza action report: who held the Katana, who acted or was role-blocked, a teammate's result. This applies even when it's offered as a 'mechanics check'. It also covers endgame faction-count arguments: 'if you hang me, only Village is left' shows you know the team count. If you need a mechanic to reconcile a result, phrase it as a hypothesis about anyone ('if someone in that pair held the Katana, they'd read Good'), never as a fact about a named player. Agree on public wording in night chat. If you slip, a vague withdrawal with no source reads as confirmation. Commit at once to one Village role that explains the knowledge (e.g. Party Animal), but first check it against every visit a living Tracker or Lookout could have seen. Move the Katana off the exposed member, and kill whoever caught the slip that night. Teammates: distance yourselves and vote with the town.

entries.tip: Once a player is shown to be Yakuza by a mechanical result (an Oracle RIGHT on a Yakuza role, a Yakuza-only role claim, a corroborated lone visit to a Katana victim), your top suspects are those who argued to delay or stop their hang, defended them, or exchanged PMs with them. A player merely caught lying is not shown Yakuza: the liar may be a Jester, and chaining from a proven liar to their early defenders lands on villagers. Nor is a player whom a lone Sheriff reads Evil: Jesters, Executioners, Ex-Cons and framed players all read Evil, so run the Jester check (t91) before treating the read as a Yakuza result. Roles stay hidden on death, so a hang never confirms who was Yakuza: keep such links only as strong as the case against the dead player. Ballots are secret, so before each nomination and trial vote, ask every player to state their vote publicly. Then compare the stated votes with the announced totals: extra No or Innocent votes mean someone hid a defensive vote. Do the vote math first. An Innocent bloc that couldn't change a settled result proves little, and Yakuza will reuse it to steer suspicion onto townies. Pushing No or delay at the nomination, then Guilty once the hang is certain, is the more telling pattern. A stated Guilty vote on a likely Yakuza clears no one. A bloc is a lead, not a verdict: a hidden investigator voting on their own info fits the same pattern, so demand a claim and results before hanging. If the game goes on after you have hanged everyone you believed Yakuza, either a Yakuza or a Neutral killer is still alive (Jesters and Executioners never block the end). Vote links to the dead then mostly point at Neutrals who voted alongside them, and a Jester wants exactly that hang. Switch to who could have made the remaining kills (causes of death, douse or attack visits), and press for claims. If you hang a likely Jester anyway, keep the Guilty votes to a bare majority.

entries.tip: If you must fake-claim, build it on info your team created, e.g. a Roleplayer or Sheriff 'Evil' result on your Fabricator's frame target. entries.tip: Blocking your kill target stops their action, not the Medic protection coming in, and never stops an attack on them. A block on the Katana's own victim is usually wasted: an investigator who dies tonight never posts tonight's result, so block the victim only to stop a same-night shot or attack (Vigilante, Enforcer). Putting your block and the Katana on one target hides a destination from Trackers, but it wastes the kill on an obvious protection target. Spend the block on the player who could stop or punish the kill (the likely Medic, a Kitsune, a Trapper about to move a trap) or on an investigator who will live to report, while the Katana hits someone else. After a failed kill, block the likely Medic (or the Vigilante or investigator) while the Katana hits someone less protected. If you also hold the Katana, you are block-immune. A claimed investigator is a prime Lookout watch target, so vary your blocks and have a cover action ready.

entries.tip: Treat the nomination and trial votes as separate decisions, unless a Clerk may hold an unused rig token. In that case a passed nomination can mean execution whatever the trial vote: vote Yes only on someone you'd accept dying, and vote No at the nomination if you are a likely target. At low player counts, don't vote Yes just to 'hear a defense'. The nominator's Yes is automatic, so don't read it as a stance. Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction or mechanical fit in their claims, votes or results, and say why an innocent explanation no longer fits. A missing result or announcement that a role-block fully explains (a blocked prosecution, an empty investigation, 'no named target') is never a contradiction; check the rules before calling one. Nor is a result that only looks false until the role's own exclusions are applied (a Juror ignores votes on either named player's nomination or trial): recompute a 'false' result from the role text before using it as your fit (t305), and remember that two claimants of a non-Unique role can both be real. A contradiction doesn't separate a Yakuza from a Jester who wants the hang. If the nominee self-nominated on any Day, voted Yes on their own nomination, asked for the rope, pushed hangs with no data, or the case rests only on behaviour (vote-steering, PMs), run the Jester check first (t91): an Evil Sheriff read on such a player is the Jester signature, not a Yakuza case. Don't let a recited 'contradiction' stand in for a mechanical case. Each of these counts as a mechanical case: a public claim of a Yakuza-only role (t227); a first-person slip about an attack or night action the player's claimed role can't make ('my Katana on Carol failed' or 'my own attacks' from a no-action claimant), which is a broken claim and not a wording quibble (t20); an unexplained Katana survival with no protector named, plus a Not Evil read and a refused night account (the Serial Killer fit, t43); an unexplained Evil result against a Vanilla claim, from a player who has not sought their own hang; a denial reversed into a role claim; a group result (survey, census, map, archive slot math) whose other members are confirmed, so elimination names the remaining player; a corroborated lone visitor to a Katana victim whose claim doesn't fit; a visit count that leaves room for only one visitor on a Katana night; slot math plus matching blocks plus a refusal to claim any role. The result behind the case must itself be corroborated: by the players it names, by a second source, or by the claimant's proven record. One unverified claimant's map, count or watch is a claim, not a mechanical fit, least of all when it was held back and names the claimant's own accuser (t296). A corroborated case plus the suspect's refusal to answer a plain yes/no about their own visit or role is enough. A bare denial offered only once cornered on trial does not answer it. 'A dodge isn't a contradiction', 'name a contradiction in my posts', 'that's only wording' and 'what exact fact has been disproved?' must not shield them. The standard is a better explanation, not proof. If you said you would vote Guilty unless they answered and they didn't, vote Guilty. Never pad a case with a fact you haven't checked: one false detail lets the defense discredit the whole push. An Evil result explained only by an uncheckable claim (Ex-Con) is not a clean acquittal: test it before trusting it. Echoed concerns and corrected slips of timeline or phrasing are not new evidence. A stated vote that doesn't fit a small trial's total is most often one miscast or misposted ballot (t211): a lead to question, not a broken claim. Three Innocent trials end the Day with no hang, so give your trials to the strongest mechanical cases and convict on them. This standard decides which case to convict, not whether to hang at all. If one more night kill could let the Yakuza block every nomination (e.g. 2 Yakuza at 4 alive), hang the best case available today, even a 50/50 group result plus a claim wobble (t286). Waiting for a perfect fit then loses the game. When no investigator is alive and no result can come, 'checkable info only' is a stall, not a standard: the best lead on the table is then your case (a pair who PM every Day, vote alike and give a vague account of the PMs, t41; the player who has made nothing checkable, t317), and it must be nominated by Day 3 at the latest. Near the lock, aim that hang at the Yakuza lead, not at a Neutral killer (t286).

In that case a passed nomination can mean execution whatever the trial vote: vote Yes only on someone you'd accept dying, and vote No at the nomination if you are a likely target. At low player counts, don't vote Yes just to 'hear a defense'. The nominator's Yes is automatic, so don't read it as a stance. Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction or mechanical fit in their claims, votes or results, and say why an innocent explanation no longer fits. A missing result or announcement that a role-block fully explains (a blocked prosecution, an empty investigation, 'no named target') is never a contradiction; check the rules before calling one. Nor is a result that only looks false until the role's own exclusions are applied (a Juror ignores votes on either named player's nomination or trial): recompute a 'false' result from the role text before using it as your fit (t305), and remember that two claimants of a non-Unique role can both be real. A contradiction doesn't separate a Yakuza from a Jester who wants the hang. If the nominee self-nominated on any Day, voted Yes on their own nomination, asked for the rope, pushed hangs with no data, or the case rests only on behaviour (vote-steering, PMs), run the Jester check first (t91): an Evil Sheriff read on such a player is the Jester signature, not a Yakuza case. Don't let a recited 'contradiction' stand in for a mechanical case. Each of these counts as a mechanical case: a public claim of a Yakuza-only role (t227); a first-person slip about an attack or night action the player's claimed role can't make ('my Katana on Carol failed' or 'my own attacks' from a no-action claimant), which is a broken claim and not a wording quibble (t20); an unexplained Katana survival with no protector named, plus a Not Evil read and a refused night account (the Serial Killer fit, t43); an unexplained Evil result against a Vanilla claim, from a player who has not sought their own hang; a denial reversed into a role claim; a group result (survey, census, map, archive slot math) whose other members are confirmed, so elimination names the remaining player; a corroborated lone visitor to a Katana victim whose claim doesn't fit; a visit count that leaves room for only one visitor on a Katana night; slot math plus matching blocks plus a refusal to claim any role. The result behind the case must itself be corroborated: by the players it names, by a second source, or by the claimant's proven record. One unverified claimant's map, count or watch is a claim, not a mechanical fit, least of all when it was held back and names the claimant's own accuser (t296). A corroborated case plus the suspect's refusal to answer a plain yes/no about their own visit or role is enough. A bare denial offered only once cornered on trial does not answer it. 'A dodge isn't a contradiction', 'name a contradiction in my posts', 'that's only wording' and 'what exact fact has been disproved?' must not shield them. The standard is a better explanation, not proof. If you said you would vote Guilty unless they answered and they didn't, vote Guilty. Never pad a case with a fact you haven't checked: one false detail lets the defense discredit the whole push. An Evil result explained only by an uncheckable claim (Ex-Con) is not a clean acquittal: test it before trusting it. Echoed concerns and corrected slips of timeline or phrasing are not new evidence. A stated vote that doesn't fit a small trial's total is most often one miscast or misposted ballot (t211): a lead to question, not a broken claim. Three Innocent trials end the Day with no hang, so give your trials to the strongest mechanical cases and convict on them. This standard decides which case to convict, not whether to hang at all. If one more night kill could let the Yakuza block every nomination (e.g. 2 Yakuza at 4 alive), hang the best case available today, even a 50/50 group result plus a claim wobble (t286). Waiting for a perfect fit then loses the game.

entries.tip: Investigators (Sheriff, Lookout, Tracker, Oracle) and protectors (Medic): never announce tonight's target in public or by private message. An announced target tells the Pharmacist or Party Animal whom to block and tells the Katana where to strike or what to avoid. Don't announce that you will act or spend a token tonight either, even with no target named ('I'll scent tonight', 'my audit will test him'): it marks you as tonight's kill. A Wiretap reads the contents of every PM, and nobody is told it exists, so treat every PM as read by the Yakuza. Never suggest another player's night target or test by PM. If someone PMs you one, don't reply confirming it; just act. Even a PM whose contents stay hidden marks you: everyone sees that it was sent, and Yakuza read a PM from one claimed investigator to another as a sign that both are worth killing. This covers only tonight's plans. Once a result exists and bears on a vote, post it in full (night, target, exact result). Never stretch secrecy about tonight into withholding or vaguening a past result, and never invent a mechanical excuse for it: Astral actions like an Oracle guess can't be seen by anyone. The one honest reason to hold a result is a possible Ritualist: an exact role claim is a sure guess through any Medic (t55), so a result that changes no vote yet can wait in your will. Narrow exception: a Trapper may announce a trap only to shield a confirmed investigator who is a likely kill target. Killers simply route around an announced trap, so it never catches anyone, and on any other player it is wasted. Otherwise keep the trap hidden and reveal it only after it fires.

entries.tip: Never put team plans (Katana holder, targets, check-dodging, claims) in daytime private messages on any Day. An Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads them word for word, and the town can publish them. Don't PM teammates at all on the first Day (Day 2). Night chat is open from Night 1, so plan there. On any Day a teammate is nominated or under pressure, send no PMs at all: even PMs to Village voters read as vote-buying, and the sender becomes the next suspect. If you must DM, summarize the content publicly at once, and never all repeat the same public explanation for your DMs. A visible PM triangle becomes the town's lead for the whole game.

If you must DM, also message villagers, and never all repeat the same public explanation for your DMs. A visible PM triangle becomes the town's lead for the whole game.

entries.tip: Map who starts PM clusters and who co-nominates. If the same few players DM each other early and then push the same nomination with no new information, treat them as a likely Yakuza bloc. Once one of them is exposed by a mechanical result, use the shared stated votes and pushes against the others. Link a PM to what happens next: if A messages B by Day and the player then under discussion (a fresh investigator claimant) dies to the Katana that night, A and B are a strong Yakuza pair. Ask sender and receiver separately, in public, for one sentence on what the PM said, compare the two answers, and don't accept a vague 'just a question': nominate one of them if no real answer comes. While mechanical results exist or are coming, a PM link is a lead, never a hang on its own, and what a PM said is never a mechanical fit. When no investigator is alive and no result is coming, a pair who PM every Day, vote identically and both claim no night action is the best case on the table: nominate one of them before the vote lock (t286) rather than a quiet solo player. Asking a claimed Lookout whom they'll watch, suggesting targets or testing a claim by PM is careless villager play that t39 warns against, not evidence of Evil. A villager who breaks that advice is still most likely a villager. A Jester or Executioner leaves PM trails on purpose: one player privately asking several others for Yes votes, or a lone early PM to a player later exposed as Yakuza, fits a Neutral as well as a Yakuza. A villager PMing for votes on a credible result is pushing clumsily. Judge the target on their own results, not on who pushes. Before hanging on a PM link or PM content while better evidence may still arrive, require stated votes that the totals back up, or a mechanical result that needs them to be a teammate. Look hard at quiet players who pile onto a PM-only hang.

entries.tip: Save the forge token for a night your target is actually likely to die (e.g. the Katana target when no protector is suspected). Roles stay hidden on death, so the town reads a forged will as the victim's own claim. It still checks the will against what the victim said while alive and against living claimants and investigators. A role claim the victim never made, a lean on a player they never suspected, or one a living counterclaimant disputes, exposes the forge and the frame. Forge something vague that fits the victim's public record: copy their public claims and add at most a mild lean they could have held. Never put a mechanics argument or a teammate's talking point in it. A will that repeats a line a suspected Yakuza already said, or a rule the table has corrected, reads as Yakuza-written and backs up the player it accuses. A forged will must fit the public transcript, and invented chronology others can check exposes you. Don't spend a frame on someone who already reads Evil (Jester, Executioner, Ex-Con). Keep your own will matching your public claim, and don't let it copy a teammate's claim word for word.

entries.tip: Survival alone confirms nothing. A power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack may be real, since Evil rarely spends its Katana on a fake, but Arsonists and Serial Killers have innate Standard Defense that stops the Katana, and Jesters and Executioners have Basic Defense. Ask the survivor at once for one claim that explains their Defense (e.g. a Medic token self-protection, a named protector or a Kitsune's charm). If no credible Medic or Kitsune claims the save, keep innate-Defense Neutrals in the pool and check the claim against token audits and visit logs. A Not Evil Sheriff read doesn't clear such a survivor: Serial Killers and Arsonists read Not Evil, so an unexplained Katana survival plus a Not Evil read is the Serial Killer signature. Add any evasion about their own night action and it is your best hang: make the case by Day 3, before the killer thins the Village. A survivor who first says 'innate Defense' or 'nobody protected me' and later claims Medic is far more likely a Neutral killer than a protected investigator. Role-blocks are different: only the blocked player is told, so 'I was blocked' is the claimant's own word and verifies nothing by itself. But it fully explains a missing result, so never treat that gap as a lie. Test the claim with an audit or a Lookout instead, and weigh repeated blocks reported before anyone pressed the claimant as mild support.

entries.tip: Never hang a claimed power role just because their action produced nothing visible: no results, no announced prosecution, 'no named target'. entries.tip: Get the mechanics right before calling something a contradiction. Night actions are optional unless a role says 'must'. Two players can claim the same role unless the rules make it unique, or unless a role list plus confirmed roles (self-proving effects, exact-role checks) accounts for every player. Once every unshown slot is filled that way, a role listed once exists exactly once, and a second claimant is a provable liar. Roles stay hidden on death, so a dead player's slot stays open unless their role was confirmed. But 'roles can repeat' only means a claim isn't disproved; it is not evidence for it. A claim of the exact role a dead victim had claimed, made by a player seen visiting that victim the night they died, is still close to a confession: weigh it with the other evidence and don't acquit on the bare possibility. Count living players and elapsed nights as of the right moment: on Day 2 only Night 1 has passed, so 'name the night of your result' is not a contradiction, and demanding it repeatedly only creates false certainty. A false 'contradiction' costs the accuser credibility, and a real one dismissed as 'roles aren't unique' frees a Yakuza.

entries.tip: When an announced trial total (Guilty plus Innocent) exceeds the number of living voters, a Ballot Stuffer doubled a vote. Ballots are secret, so compare each side's total with the players who said they voted that way. The side with more votes than stated holds the extra vote, or a hidden liar. The extra vote can sit on either side, including the losing side and the nominee's own Innocent vote. This narrows the stuffer to that side's voters; it doesn't name one. Separate the candidates using each one's stated position against the totals, plus any token or claim evidence (an audit sees ballot tokens), before hanging. Once a mechanical result identifies the stuffer, stop treating the other candidates as mechanically implicated.

entries.tip: A clean token is spent even if the target survives. Roles are hidden on death, so a clean hides the victim's last will: it shows as 'cleaned by mortician', and you privately learn their role and will. It also blocks a Coroner, who learns nothing from a cleaned body. The public notice proves a Mortician exists. Clean only when the kill is near-certain (no possible Defense, no likely protector) and the will or body likely holds something that hurts your team: an investigator who has probably checked you, a puppeting notice, or one side of a claim duel a Coroner would examine. A clean of a player whose results are already public saves little. Don't add your clean visit to another Yakuza's Katana target while a Lookout may watch; clean only when you hold the Katana yourself or the visit is expendable.

entries.tip: While a Ritualist may be alive with tokens, every firm exact-role claim (Archivist, Eavesdropper, Bloodhound, Juror, Seer) is a near-certain extra kill on top of the Katana, through any Medic. A wrong guess outs the Ritualist publicly and its tokens are spent either way, so it waits for sure claims: first-turn claims of roles a Roleplayer can't be told (anything except Sheriff, Tracker, Lookout, Seer, Fortune Teller, Oracle, Accountant) backed by a result that fits known facts. A living Diviner also feeds it exact roles, and a Wiretap reads private claims. Survey or archive results can pin a survivor's role indirectly. entries.tip: Do the trial math in night chat. Spend a token only on a Day when your doubled vote can change an outcome, e.g. near half: a doubled Innocent makes trials need more Guilty than the Village has (7 alive means 8 counted, so 5 Guilty are needed). A bare-majority hang (4 of 7) becomes a failing tie with your extra vote. Nomination votes aren't doubled. Vote the way you said you would publicly: the extra vote narrows suspects to voters on that side, and a stance/ballot mismatch names you.

entries.tip: An archive or partial survey is a sample, not a census. It shows that roles exist, never how many. Never say a duplicate claim 'proves' a liar. Say instead that it shifts the odds, e.g. 'only half the archive's entries are real, so three Vanilla claims against one listed Vanilla are worth testing'. Overstating the math gets a correct suspicion discredited and the trial acquitted. Once a list is public, keep a role inventory every Day and post it. The list is one claimant's report until something corroborates it. Of the N roles shown, floor(0.5*N) are real and the rest are fakes that may or may not be in the game. So a listed role may be absent, and a role listed once may have an unsampled second holder. Use slot math to decide whom to press for an exact claim and whom to audit, watch or guess. Then hang on the contradiction that test produces (e.g. a token count against a Vanilla claim, an Evil check), not on slot math alone. Roles proven by public effects (a prosecution proves a Prosecutor, a clean a Mortician, an ignite an Arsonist) are certain. Track Unique roles (Smuggler, Vulture) separately: once one is proven, every other living claimant of it is a proven liar. A claim made right after a result that only explains that result is not placed, so keep it open. When the inventory narrows to a few unclaimed players, demand an exact claim from each; a refusal then is heavy evidence. Late in the game an unverified 'Vanilla' claim is worth testing early. Keep deductions conditional: corroborating one entry doesn't verify the whole list.

Assign at most that many off-list claims across the whole team, and never put two members in one slot or both on Vanilla. Never fake-claim a role the list shows once while its holder may be alive, and never a Unique role (Vulture, Smuggler) whose holder may be alive: their counterclaim disproves you for free. A cover that fits your tokens and visits can still collide with a real holder: a duplicated claim, like a Vanilla claim, is the first thing an Oracle guesses, and one WRONG ends it. If a real holder counterclaims, expect the test that night and kill the likeliest exact-role checker (t294) rather than hoping the duel stays open. Roles stay hidden on death, so a listed role whose known claimant is dead is the safest choice. Pick it early and keep it: switching claims once cornered is fatal.

entries.tip: Plan the endgame around exact vote math. Parity doesn't end the game. At 2v2, vote No on every nomination (none can reach a majority), kill one villager at night, then nominate and hang the last at 2-1. Before risky night trades, pre-agree exactly whom the survivors kill and how they vote.

entries.tip: Once you claim Veteran publicly, Yakuza will avoid you, so later alerts mostly catch Village visitors (Medics, Lookouts) instead. Claim when it confirms a kill or saves a lynch, ideally after your best alerts are used. Never announce future alert nights or how many tokens you have left: it tells evil when you are safe to visit and only endangers your own side. When you do claim, give your full past alert record (each night, visitors or none) in one message and keep it fixed. A record that grows a night each Day looks invented even when it's true. If you are claimed, tell the Village publicly never to visit you.

entries.tip: If someone else claims your role, counterclaim at once with details only the real holder has (token count, shot reasoning) and put the claim in your will. Vigilante isn't Unique, so the other claimant may be real too: a claim clash alone is never the lead for a shot. Test them with a vote, a Sheriff check or an audit, and shoot them only once another result breaks their claim (a token count that doesn't fit, a claimed shot that matches no death). Then use at least a Standard shot (2 tokens) in case they have Defense, that same night. The counterclaim names your exact role, so expect the Katana, or a Ritualist guess that no Medic stops, right after it, and have your best-lead shot queued.

entries.tip: Stay quiet and never hint publicly that a Wiretap exists. The Village's own fear of a Wiretap often shuts down PM evidence for you. Never quote or closely paraphrase a PM: a quote proves you read it, and the two people in that exchange will ask how. entries.tip: Fortune Teller numbers are labeled: players visited (distinct) and players who visited anyone (distinct). Every visiting action counts, including Lookout watches, Tracker tracks, Accountant audits, Medic protections, Fabricator frames and the Katana. Self-visits count in both. A Veteran's alert isn't a visit, but anyone who visits the Veteran is. Blocked and Astral actions (Oracle, Ritualist, ignite, map, Coroner exam, Jester or Executioner revenge) count in neither. Players who died that night still count. One visitor can add several destinations: a Katana holder who also uses their own visiting action, a Smuggler (a swap visits both players) or a Seer's chosen pair (visits both). Read small counts literally. On a night with a Katana death, a visitor total of 1 means the holder made every visit that night. Anyone who claims a visit that night is then the holder or is lying, and a player who refuses to state their night action, or gives only a bare denial, is the hang. A totals-only role can't name visitors, so 'the FT's visitors are unnamed' is not a flaw, and evil uses that line to hang a real FT. FT: line your totals up publicly against every claimed visit, then ask each player with no claimed action for a plain yes/no on the leftover visit. A total that doesn't fit shows that some set of claims is false, not which claim. List every account that repairs it (holder acting twice, a swap, a chosen Seer pair, Ex-Con random visit, douses, switched plans). Outside the one-visitor case, never hang on the count alone, least of all against an exact-role check. Ask for the totals per night and the derivation before calling a count a lie.

history.old: Fortune Teller numbers are unordered. One counts players visited; the other counts players who visited someone ELSE, so self-targets are excluded. One visitor can cover two targets, e.g. a Katana holder who also uses their own action. Equal numbers therefore don't prove nobody was double-visited. Before using a count, list every way it could fit: a holder acting twice, Ex-Con random visits, Arsonist douses, self-protects, and players who switched from a 'plan' in their will. A count that doesn't fit is weak evidence. Never hang on it alone, least of all against a claim backed by an exact-role check or a flip.

entries.tip: When a Clerk rig is announced, the Yakuza wanted that nominee dead. Treat the nominator, the players who pushed the nomination and everyone who said they voted Guilty on that trial as prime suspects. Ballots are secret, so compare the Guilty total with the stated votes to find hidden Guilty voters. Hang from that group next. Don't drift back to old suspects.

entries.tip: (Yakuza) Use one-shot Day tokens (Clerk rig, puppet, Mortician clean) early, on the first Day they can swing a vote, and before their holder is exposed. Don't wait for a 'decisive day': holders who keep saving them die with them unused. Combine them when you can. Rig so that any nomination you can pass kills a Villager, puppet a trusted villager to push it, and kill and clean the puppet that night so their will can't expose it. Once you hold a voting majority, stop arguing and vote as a bloc, and hang the most dangerous town role first (e.g. a Veteran). A puppet lapses if you die the night you spend it (R21), so spend it at least a night before a likely death. Never rig a Day when you or a teammate is the likely nominee, because the rig executes your own side.

entries.tip: As a solo killer you win only alone. Douse or kill the suspected Yakuza bloc first: players whose stated votes line up on every key hang, who defended an exposed Yakuza and who lead pushes on proven town roles. A doused Yakuza is told an Arsonist doused them, and the team shares it in night chat. Each Yakuza douse puts the team's votes and any Ritualist on your trail, so douse them late in your cycle and ignite soon after. The Standard Katana can't get through your Standard Defense, so the Yakuza's weapons against you are the hang and a Ritualist's Divine guess. If you wipe out the Village and leave several Yakuza alive, they outvote and hang you; a final two against one Yakuza with no ritual tokens is yours. In a small endgame your role is easy to deduce by elimination, so finish the Yakuza while you still can.

entries.tip: Accurate information proves access, not alignment. A Diviner can post real role results as a 'Surveyor', a Wiretap can quote real private messages as an 'Eavesdropper', and an evil player can truthfully expose a rival killer. A visiting killer can also present their own real visits (douses, a Katana hit) as 'Tracker' tracks, which then fit Fortune Teller counts and Cartographer groups perfectly. A fit with visit totals shows that the visits happened, not who made them or why. Before clearing an info claimer, ask which hostile role could produce the same evidence. Then look for a check that tells them apart: an Oracle guess, an Accountant audit, or a Lookout on the claimant's target. An exact-role result from an investigator with a proven record outweighs visit-count consistency. Confirming one detail authenticates only that detail. When such a claimer is exposed as hostile, re-examine everyone they cleared, but don't hang the subjects of their true reads just because they were 'confirmed' by them.

entries.tip: Your results look exactly like a Surveyor's, so informed towns treat a Surveyor claim as the Diviner's twin. Accurate hits don't clear it. An Oracle guess on your claim or a profile of you breaks it (your true role is always on your own profile list), a Diviner entry on an archive or on someone else's profile points the town at it, and an Accountant sees your 0 tokens against a Surveyor's 3. Prefer a tokenless visiting cover (Lookout, Tracker, Sheriff) that names your real divine targets as its targets, and share your draws with the team in night chat instead of publishing them. If you do use Surveyor, publish a few accurate, harmless groups early and put a plausible other suspect in front of the town. Divine teammates who must visit risky targets: Strong Defense stops traps and Vigilante shots. A token gifted to you is thrown away.

entries.tip: Guess the public role claims of suspicious or load-bearing players. Best is a freshly made or switched claim, above all a power claim made after a map or count put the player in a suspect group. Also good: defenders of exposed Yakuza, and cheap Vanilla claims. A WRONG exposes a fake at once, and nobody can say you copied it. A RIGHT on an already-public claim proves little to others, since a fake Oracle could invent it. So aim confirming guesses where they unlock another result: a RIGHT on one member of a census or group result lets elimination name the rest. Post a result as soon as it bears on a vote or a claim dispute; holding one that matters while others claim makes you the next suspect. The claim names your exact role to a possible Ritualist, so when one may be in the game a result that changes nothing yet can wait in your will. When you post, give every result in one message: night, target, exact role guessed, RIGHT or WRONG (e.g. 'N4: guessed Heidi = Tracker, WRONG'). A bare 'X is not a Tracker' sounds evasive. Your guess is Astral, so no 'exposure' excuse applies, but a swap still moves it: if your target posts a swap notice for that night, the result describes the other swapped player. Give a stated reason with every nomination, argue for a Vigilante shot in public rather than by PM, and keep your planned next guess in your will. Once confirmed, assume you die tonight and keep your will hedged.

entries.tip: Give tokens only to roles verified by something other than their own claim. Best is a role confirmed by public effects whose token pays off by day, e.g. a Prosecutor whose announced prosecutions hit players later caught by mechanical results. Never announce whom you plan to gift. Don't gift a player likely to die that night, such as one who just announced a night action: a gift to a dead player confirms nothing and looks invented. Don't sit on both tokens waiting for certainty either. You're never told if the token was thrown away, so a fake claimer can just 'confirm' the gift, and your credibility gets tied to theirs. Your gift is a visit, so a claimed Fortune Teller or Cartographer must account for it, which can test their claim. A swap can redirect a gift without telling you.

entries.tip: Jester warnings: suspect a Jester in a player who pushes hard with no evidence, self-nominates 'as a test', votes Yes on their own nomination (or misstates that vote), refuses offered tests of their own result, or makes a lone, easily disproved claim that contradicts a well-supported report and seems eager to be tried. A typical case is jumping onto a survey or archive pool's role so the real holder counterclaims. Track the conversion: if an archive lists Executioner and anyone has died at night, an Executioner whose target that was is now a Jester. An Evil Sheriff result on a Vanilla claimant with 0 tokens fits a Jester or Executioner as well as a Yakuza. An Evil read on a player who self-nominates or won't prove their claim is the Jester signature: a Yakuza who reads Evil doesn't ask for the rope. A self-nomination is never a reason to vote Guilty. A mild early dissent plus a lone PM to a player later exposed as Yakuza doesn't rule a Jester out. A caught liar is a liar, not necessarily a Yakuza, and reckless, checkable lies are what a Jester tells. If a more clearly Yakuza player is available, hang them first. While the Katana still kills, don't spend the Day on a proven liar who doesn't fit as a killer. Before any hang, ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged, and if so prefer to leave them alive. Naming the Jester risk aloud and then voting Guilty anyway is the worst of both. If you must hang, agree in public on a bare majority of Guilty votes and have everyone else vote Innocent. The revenge Divine-attacks a random Guilty voter, and no protection stops it. Confirmed power roles (Medic, investigators, a Prosecutor with tokens) must vote Innocent, and so must anyone with the Cursed trait (R24), whose curse would kill a second Good player.

Track the conversion: if an archive lists Executioner and anyone has died at night, an Executioner whose target that was is now a Jester. An Evil Sheriff result on a Vanilla claimant with 0 tokens fits a Jester or Executioner as well as a Yakuza. A mild Day 1 dissent plus a lone PM to a player later exposed as Yakuza doesn't rule a Jester out. A caught liar is a liar, not necessarily a Yakuza. If a more clearly Yakuza player is available, hang them first. Before any hang, ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged, and if so prefer to leave them alive. If you must hang, agree in public on a bare majority of Guilty votes and have everyone else vote Innocent. The revenge Divine-attacks a random Guilty voter, and no protection stops it. Confirmed power roles (Medic, investigators, a Prosecutor with tokens) must vote Innocent.
history.note: Revision: 'Day 1 dissent' is now 'early dissent', since there is no Day 1.

entries.tip: Build a hard, Village-sounding case. A fake investigative counterclaim against a credible info role (e.g. a fake Tracker result contradicting a Lookout's list) is a fast route to a hang. A passive counting claim (Cartographer, Fortune Teller) with a bold, falsifiable result posted before anyone speaks ('one visit all night') works well: the real visitors contradict you, and the town reads a duel, not a Jester. You needn't hang on Day 2. Escalate into a specific accusation. If a Villager hangs on it, the night's events break your claim and the town hangs the 'proven liar' the next Day. Being the obvious next hang also keeps the Katana off you, which your Basic Defense wouldn't stop. Commit to the claim and reject the Roleplayer excuse the town offers. On trial, fight: accuse your accusers and say you vote Innocent while voting Guilty. One small checkable lie (a secret Yes on your own nomination, stated as No) tips waverers, but careful players read it as a Jester tell, so don't overdo it. A self-nomination framed as a 'test' can also work, but repeated self-nominations or an open Jester claim make the town refuse to hang you.

entries.tip: Never flatly deny a night visit that any visit result could expose: a Lookout or Tracker log, a Cartographer or Scout group, or a Fortune Teller count. The Katana holder always shares a group with the victim. Once a Cartographer, Scout or FT is claimed, assume the kill visit can be isolated to a few names. Agree a plausible cover action in night chat before Day starts. If you are asked or a visit is exposed, admit it at once with that cover. A denial followed by a reversal is far more damning than the visit itself. Don't publicly endorse a Village player's account of a night when you visited the same target (e.g. backing a Medic's protection claim on your Katana target). A cover revealed later then reads as a second, invented claim.

entries.tip: Never announce your protection target, in public or by private message (a Wiretap reads PMs). Don't claim Medic or name your ward before a trial or a survival question needs it: a named Medic is who a Pharmacist blocks on every kill night, and a block stops all your protection, self-protection included. If you are told you were role-blocked, a blocker has read your pattern: change wards, and post the notice once it bears on a death (if no Village blocker claims it, a Pharmacist is alive). Free Standard protection stops the Katana but not a Strong attack (Serial Killer, Arsonist ignite, a 3-token shot, a Veteran's alert, a trap). Hold your Strong tokens while only the Katana threatens, and spend them on a confirmed investigator as soon as a Strong attacker is credible (t8). While the Katana still kills, keep one token for a Standard self-protection: at 0 tokens you can't protect yourself. Don't protect the same claimed player in an obvious nightly pattern. A Pharmacist can block it, and a Smuggler can aim the Katana at a decoy and swap the decoy with your ward, which moves your save onto the decoy and the kill onto your ward. A Divine Ritualist guess beats any protection, so a lone claimed Medic should expect one.

entries.tip: If a teammate is likely to be checked by a Sheriff tonight, give them the Katana so they read Good. This matters most on the night after they were nominated, tried or publicly suspected, or when the table has asked the Sheriff aloud to check them. An idle Grunt gains nothing by keeping it by default. Pair it with a block on the known protector. Weigh this against the visit risk if a Lookout or Tracker is active, and against an Enforcer: the holder is the one player an Enforcer's visit kills, and a publicly suspected teammate is exactly whom an Enforcer visits. If a likely Enforcer is alive (t329), block them that night or leave the Katana on an unsuspected member and accept the Evil read.

entries.tip: If the last known Yakuza dies and the game doesn't end, a Neutral is still alive. Count the players, check the Vulture threshold (max(floor(N/4),2)) and look hard at the weakest or latest claim. Don't hang a player who says they are Cursed (a trait, R24) near the endgame: their death Divine-attacks a random Good player at the end of the following night and can hand a Vulture the win. No investigation sees traits, so the claim can't be checked; look at who is pushing that hang and count the worst case before voting.

entries.tip: Claim a plain, tokenless no-action role early (Vanilla works when no Oracle or exact-role checker is active, and it matches an audit of 0) and keep it word for word. Vote with the majority and never lead a push or nominate: both killing factions then leave you for last, and the count runs down to your threshold by itself. Never copy a role whose actions were already public or whose real holder may be among the unclaimed. If someone fake-claims your Unique role, counterclaim or open a private deal with them that Day. Avoid vouching for players, lone Guilty votes and aggressive endgame nominations, especially of a player who has said they are Cursed (the hang plus the curse is an obvious count drop). Count the threshold, max(floor(N/4),2) alive at the start of a Day, after every death. In the endgame, don't push a hang or vote that would let the town notice the count is about to hand you the win.

entries.tip: Judge a Roleplayer claim by its timing and consistency. A Roleplayer is told a fake investigative role and believes it: they claim that role from the start, never claim Vanilla, and never 'know' they are a Roleplayer. They can only suspect it, once their results clash with a confirmed claim or result (an exact-role check, a self-proving action, a verified log). A real one flags the clash early, before others claim the slot, and pushes against other Roleplayer claimants. A Vanilla claim that later becomes Roleplayer, an 'I know I'm the Roleplayer', or a claim made only once cornered or prosecuted is almost certainly a lie. When two players claim the same investigative role and their results conflict, consider an honest Roleplayer before calling either one a liar. If an archive, profile or survey shows 'Roleplayer', the duplicate claim may need no Evil player at all. Discount the claimant with the odder, unverifiable result instead of spending the Day hanging them, keep the other claimant's results, and spend the hang on the unclaimed pool. entries.tip: Your claim is self-proving: the prosecution is announced the next Day, and Yakuza can't fake it. Stay unclaimed while your tokens are live. Spend each prosecution as soon as a solid mechanical lead exists, while enough Village voters are alive to win the trial. If you hold tokens for the endgame, the Katana removes your voters first and you may die with them unused. Good leads: a public claim of a Yakuza-only role, the slip or PM partner of a player exposed by a mechanical result, the player who defended or stated Innocent on a hanged near-certain Yakuza, a claim that overflows a public role list, a player in a confirmed visitor list, or a small Guilty total on a proven townie that the stated votes don't account for. Never spend one on a claimant whose results keep checking out (e.g. an Oracle with a verified hit), or on a result you call false without recomputing it from the role text (t305). An acquittal wastes the token and one of the Day's three trials, and an execution ends the Day: at 4-5 alive a wrong prosecution uses up the Village's last real hang, so double-check the lead before the night. A prosecution skips the nomination vote, so No votes can't stall it. Before each prosecution, name the target as a suspect in public that Day, but don't announce that you will prosecute tonight: a Pharmacist will block you. Log each prosecution in your will by NIGHT (N2, N3), not by trial day. If a copycat counterclaims, those earlier reads and correct labels are your proof. If you are role-blocked, you are told and no token is spent. If you have already claimed, post 'N3: prosecution of X was role-blocked' in your first message the next Day, before anyone can call the missing trial a bluff, and ask an Accountant to confirm your token count. If you are still unclaimed, keep the block in your will instead: a Prosecutor claim names your exact role to a possible Ritualist, whose guess no Medic stops. Under R21 the prosecution still fires even if you die that night, so spend your last token on your top suspect even when you expect to be killed.

entries.tip: A random-pair result only compares two appearances. Chain it once either player is anchored as Good by an independent source (a Sheriff Not Evil plus an Oracle RIGHT on a Village role, a self-proving action, a verified log). Chain again when an exact-role check (a Coroner exam, an Oracle guess) confirms a hanged player's role. Before calling anyone cleared or caught, check the exceptions: the Katana holder reads Good that night, an Ex-Con reads Evil, and a framed player reads Evil. A DIFFERENT pair doesn't say which member is which. Spend your chosen-pair token on one anchored-Good player plus a suspect. Never spend it on a pair that includes the likely holder, above all when only one Yakuza can be left: that player reads Good every night, so a SAME result with them proves nothing and never means 'both Yakuza'.

entries.tip: A rig bypasses the acquittal, not the nomination. Use it on a non-teammate who can get a nomination majority but probably not a Guilty majority. entries.tip: Choose blocks by the damage they prevent. Block the strongest Katana-holder suspect every night: a player a Lookout or Tracker saw at a victim, the last living name an elimination map allows, or late in the game the likeliest lone holder. Keep blocking that suspect every night until they are hanged. Switching away hands them a free kill, often on you. The same works on a Neutral-killer suspect: a quiet night after your block is a mechanical result. The Katana passes to a teammate when its holder dies, so re-check who likely holds it after every death. Before you have a suspect, use blocks as tests on claimed Vanillas and quiet players, or block a player likely to confirm it publicly and credibly (an investigator about to claim): a block confirmed by a trusted target is what separates you from a Pharmacist making the same claim. You are told only whether the block failed because the target can't be role-blocked. Such a failure shows an immune role (Pharmacist, Smuggler, Veteran or Party Animal). Report every block in the moderator's exact wording ('did not fail because of immunity'), never 'my block landed': a loose phrase gets attacked as a mechanics error. A no-kill night that matches your block is the town's strongest lead against a lone holder. Write each block target in your will before the night. Post the log publicly, before anyone can confirm it, once it bears on a claim, a no-kill night or a vote: a target who later confirms being blocked proves you are real. Posting names your exact role to a possible Ritualist, whose guess no Medic stops, so when one may be in the game don't post a log that shows nothing yet. Never block a protector or investigator confirmed by an independent source, and avoid blocking quiet players who defended confirmed claims, who may be a hidden Vigilante or Enforcer: a blocked killer makes no attack, so your block also cancels an Enforcer's visit to the same suspect. A persistent liar who keeps showing no visits may be an Executioner, and blocking them prevents nothing.

Put it on a claimed investigator or other info role the killers must visit, never on a suspect: nobody attacks a Yakuza, so a trap there stays silent and clears no one. So moving it to a player in danger tonight protects nobody tonight: the new ward is uncovered and the old one is open. Once you have an armed trap on a player the killers may hit, leave it there. If the killers know where it is and stay away, it is already working. If you do move it, never say so: that tells the killers the old ward is free. The trap persists through your death and through role-blocks on you. Trapper isn't Unique, so a second claimant may be real. A trap placed on a player who died that same night was still a legal placement (night actions resolve together), so don't call a rival's trap 'impossible' without checking the rules.

entries.tip: Weigh a visit report by when it was made, but only together with confirmation. A count posted first that the real visitors contradict gains nothing from its timing. A list or counter-result that only repeats public claims is weak. entries.tip: Once you have claimed, post your automatic random pair every night in your first speech, with the night and 'random' or 'chosen', even when it seems useless. entries.tip: Cross group results (Surveyor, Diviner, census-type alignment counts) with token audits, confirmed roles and independently corroborated claims to eliminate candidates. A nonzero token count rules out tokenless roles (Arsonist, Serial Killer, Jester, Grunt, Vanilla). A confirmed role removes that player. A death doesn't: roles stay hidden, so a dead member is still a candidate for the night's group. A 'k of 3 Good' count becomes a named suspect once the other members are confirmed: nominate and vote on it rather than waiting for a direct contradiction. Remember that an alignment count reads true alignment, so a non-Good slot may be a Neutral, not a Yakuza. A player's own claim is a claim, not corroboration. State which reports the elimination depends on, then press the last candidate. A Vanilla claim doesn't explain a survey slot.

entries.tip: Don't play clean. Voting with confirmed town and claiming Vanilla gives you no route to a hanging, and a town with confirmed power roles will hang real Evil instead of you. entries.tip: Before accepting a chain of claims that corroborate each other, list which links are independently verified. Verified links include a self-proving action, a token audit, a tracked visit, an Oracle check, a survived attack that matches a Medic's claimed protection, and a block notice confirmed by its target. A chain with no verified link is a story, not evidence. Name which single link could be tested tonight and what would still follow if it were false. Don't swing to ignoring the map, though. If its links hold up and it leaves one living candidate, that candidate stays the top case. Don't acquit them and then spend the hang on someone whose checkable record is clean but whose nominations misfired. If you won't hang the candidate today, block or track them that night.

entries.tip: (If you have the Cursed trait) Keep the trait hidden while safe. No investigation sees traits, so it comes out only if you say it. Your curse hits only Good players, so to the Yakuza you are a two-for-one kill. Claim your role as normal, but write 'I am Cursed' in your will so the town reads the random Good death (cause 'a curse') correctly. Never vote Guilty on a nominee who might be a Jester or an Executioner's target: if the revenge draw hits you, your curse kills a second Good player. Vote Innocent, give the Jester risk as your reason, and let others carry the hang. If a Vigilante may shoot you or the Village is about to hang you, say you are Cursed at once. It can't be verified and it tells the Yakuza you are worth two kills, so say it only when the alternative is a Village kill.

entries.tip: While a Serial Killer or Arsonist is alive, hang them at the first chance, even if that means voting alongside the Village. The Standard Katana never gets through their Standard Defense (only a Ritualist's 2-token Divine guess does), while their Strong attack or ignite kills any of you, so a final two against one is a loss. Do the count as soon as a cause of death shows the killer exists, not in the final three. When the town is set to hang a rival Neutral killer, add your Guilty votes: it removes the one player you can't kill, keeps your record clean, and uses up the town's hang on a non-Yakuza. If you can't yet tell which of two unclaimed players is the killer, hang one of them rather than a claimed Village power role: a Villager hanged while the killer lives leaves you the duel you can't win. A Katana that fails on a player no protector covers names the killer (t45). Never vote to save the killer in order to hang a Villager in a small endgame. Count ahead: with the killer hanged, your next night kill can leave you one against one with a Villager, where you vote No on every nomination and the Katana finishes it.

entries.tip: Never visit a claimed, contested or likely Veteran at night: no protections, no watches, no audits. A Veteran's alert Strong-attacks every visitor whatever their faction. The Yakuza visit by choice and simply stay away, so the only players a known Veteran kills are your own Medic and investigators. A Veteran on alert already has Standard Defense, so protecting them gains nothing. Above all, never visit on a night the Veteran said they would alert. To verify a Veteran, use visit-free or Astral checks, or wait for their alert reports. If a Veteran hasn't claimed, ask them to claim first, or coordinate so that at most one investigator takes the risk.

entries.tip: A night with no Katana kill right after a blocker hit player X is a lead that X holds the Katana. Verify the blocker first: the blocked player confirms the block publicly, earlier blocks were confirmed by independent players, or the only other blocker role (Pharmacist) is already exposed by a mechanical result. A lone holder can skip a night on purpose to frame the block target, and a kill can also fail to protection, so one match is weak. Two or more matches with a confirmed blocker log is a real mechanical case to hang on, and so is one match plus an exact-role result that breaks X's claim (an Oracle WRONG on their claimed role). Ask what each side would have done: at 4 alive a Yakuza pair would have killed and then held the vote, and an unblocked lone holder had a kill available, so a quiet night there points at the blocked player and rules out 'the blocker and X are a pair'. Once a public role list (archive, survey) shows Yakuza roles, guess the roles still unaccounted for against the top suspects; a listed Grunt narrowed by slot math is a good guess. entries.tip: Don't kill Yakuza early: each one you remove strengthens a large town against you. That includes players with duplicate or suspicious claims (a second Tracker whose result neatly matches a blocker's): they are often Yakuza, and they do your killing for you. Hit Village power roles that can read or stop you. A claimed Oracle comes first: a Sheriff reads you Not Evil, but once elimination narrows the killer to two or three players one 'Serial Killer' guess ends you. Then claimed Trackers and Lookouts, blockers, the Accountant, an Enforcer and a Kitsune holding a swallowed Strong attack. Watch who is being cleared: a player confirmed blocked on a night you killed is struck from the list, so a working blocker shrinks the pool onto you; kill or discredit them before it reaches two names. A claimed Sheriff is no threat to you and the Yakuza will kill them anyway: leave them to the Katana. Don't attack the player the Yakuza obviously want dead (e.g. a Lookout who just exposed their holder, a freshly claimed investigator); a double kill wastes your night, and if a protector stops it the victim and a Kitsune both learn a Serial Killer attacked. Read each night's causes of death to see where the Katana goes. Don't volunteer a Vanilla claim early when nobody pressed you; it is the first claim exact-role checkers test once SK kills appear. But don't sit silent and unclaimed for Days either: the quiet player with a late Vanilla claim is the easy nominee, and the Yakuza will lead that hang to be rid of you. Take a visible stance from Day 2 (a named suspect with a reason) and answer the first direct question in one plain sentence (t188). On a small table, count: once the Yakuza need only one Village vote to hang you, push the visible Yakuza lead (e.g. a PM pair) yourself before they nominate you. Turn on the Yakuza only when the town is small. Plan the endgame on Defense: the Standard Katana can't get through your Standard Defense, so the Yakuza can only hang you or hit you with a Ritualist's Divine guess. A final two with the last Yakuza is a win if they hold no ritual tokens. At four or five alive, let the Yakuza and the Village hang each other, quietly add your vote to a push on a Villager rather than defending anyone, and at two alive vote No on every nomination and kill. Ballots are secret, so you can state a cautious lean and cast the vote that thins the field, but at 5 or fewer alive the totals can show whose stated vote was false (t239).

entries.tip: A publicly announced trap on a confirmed investigator deters killers, who will route around that player, so it works like protection. But a lone holder simply avoids the predictable target, so a hidden trap is the one that actually catches someone: choose between deterrence and catching. Traps arm only from the next night, so aim at whoever the Katana is likely to hit in two nights. A silent trap also gives free negative info: report it as 'no non-Village visitor to X'. If a Lookout reveals your visit to a victim, claim at once with mechanics others can check. Any Trapper claim names your exact role to a possible Ritualist, so claim no earlier than a sighting or a vote forces it.

entries.tip: Audit claimed tokenless visitors and quiet unclaimed players. When posting, state which roles the count rules in and out rather than only the raw number: a raw 3 can out a hidden Vigilante. A 0 rules out an unspent Medic, Vigilante, Veteran or Prosecutor but fits Jester, Executioner, SK and Vanilla, so say so. A 3 fits Village roles (Vigilante, Veteran, Surveyor, Coroner, Profiler) but also a Yakuza Mortician or Talent Agent, so it clears nobody on its own. entries.tip: Never claim a role that exists only on the Yakuza side (Mortician, Clerk, Diviner, Puppeteer, Ballot Stuffer, Wiretap, Pharmacist, Ritualist, etc.), whether as a fake claim or as the truth. When asked about your night actions, answer with that prepared claim in one plain sentence.

entries.tip: A Cursed player's curse (a trait, R24) Divine-attacks a random living Good player, so killing one costs the Village two players. Don't avoid a player who has revealed they are Cursed as 'dangerous'. Read each death-trigger trait to see which side it punishes: Cursed hits only Good players, while Avenger kills every player whose attack was fatal, i.e. your Katana holder, and a Ritualist whose guess hit the same target that night. No investigation sees traits, so any night kill on a Villager can cost you the attacker: keep the Katana on the member you can best afford to lose, never on one holding unspent one-shot tokens, and don't stack two killers on one target. An 'Avenger' cause of death also names the dead Yakuza as the attacker in public, so the town turns to their PM partners and to any teammate whose claim the victim disputed. Count the curse as a second kill when you choose a Katana target.

entries.tip: In an endgame of three with a Jester alive (a killer, which may be the last Yakuza or a solo Neutral, plus a Villager and the Jester), the Jester's vote decides every trial. Hanging the Jester gives him his win and removes no killer, and the killer then kills the last Villager that night. Village: never vote Guilty on the Jester there. Make the killer's hang the only goal and win the Jester's vote by negotiating, not with ultimatums. Pass his self-nominations early (a Yes only starts the trial), so the killer must vote publicly on any hang he promised, and expose a broken promise while you still have votes. If the numbers allow hanging the Jester without leaving you alone with the killer, that is also an option, because his win doesn't block yours. Killer: you can buy the Jester's Innocent by promising a Guilty on his next self-nomination, but weigh the revenge draw on Guilty voters.

entries.tip: Assume a freshly claimed investigator is both protected by the Medic and watched by a Lookout. Never send the Katana at a player a Lookout or Tracker has publicly said they will watch. entries.tip: Check every claimed neighbor-group result (Surveyor, Diviner) against the circle as it stood at the start of that night. Remove the dead, skip the user's own seat, and walk both directions to the nearest eligible player. Write the steps out publicly. A group with the wrong neighbors exposes a fake claim at once, and it is a clean mechanical contradiction. A Census Taker's group is different: its target plus two players drawn at random from everyone else alive, so no seating check applies to it. A wrong 'impossible' call puts a true investigator on trial and costs the accuser credibility the Yakuza will use later, so get the steps right before calling it.

entries.tip: Once you have claimed, post your nightly group sizes in your first speech every Day, labeled by night. A Cartographer claim is a sure guess for a possible Ritualist (no Roleplayer is told it). When one may be in the game, make your first post on a Day when the sizes or a map bear on a death or a claim, and have the whole log in your will first. Before posting any deduction from the sizes, place every claimed visit and put yourself correctly. Then post once and never revise in public: each correction hands the Yakuza a 'his lists keep changing' defense. Spend map tokens on the player likeliest to be killed tonight (the strongest confirmed info role, or a Lookout whose result just decided a hang). If they die, the map names everyone linked to the Katana visit and cuts the holder to a handful; cross it with the FT counts the next morning. Post a map result (named group) as soon as you have it, before the mapped player's visit claim is tested. Write tonight's planned map target in your will, because a map result from the night you die never reaches it. Don't announce in public whom you'll map or how many map tokens you have left: it tells the Yakuza to move the Katana, swap, or kill you. A group shows who is linked, not who visited whom, so pair it with a Lookout or Tracker report, or with elimination of the confirmed members, before naming a holder.

entries.tip: Cartographer and Scout groups are undirected. A Katana kill puts the holder in the victim's group that night, but the group alone doesn't say who attacked whom. First narrow the holder to the group's members. Then eliminate: remove the victim, any member confirmed as no-action (by an Oracle RIGHT on Vanilla or another exact-role check) whose link the victim's own visit can explain, and any member with a corroborated harmless visit. If only one unconfirmed member is left, treat them as the likely holder and act that Day, especially if they dodge a plain yes/no about their own visit. 'A link isn't a visit' and 'test it from outside the group first' must not acquit that last member. Use a direction-aware result (Lookout, Tracker) only when elimination doesn't finish the job.

entries.tip: Know which actions are Astral: Oracle and Ritualist guesses, the Juror's and Scrutineer's checks, the Arsonist's ignite, the Cartographer's map, the Coroner's exam, and the Jester's and Executioner's revenge attacks. No Lookout, Tracker, Fortune Teller, Insomniac, trap, Veteran or Katana holder can see or react to them. 'My target would be exposed' is never a reason to withhold an Astral result. A Smuggler's swap is different: it moves every action aimed at a swapped living player, Astral ones included. An Oracle guess, a Juror pair, a Scrutineer pick, a map or a Ritualist guess aimed at one swapped player lands on the other and is reported under the chosen name. Only random-draw effects (a Jester's or Executioner's revenge, a Cursed player's curse) are not moved. Yakuza: an Oracle isn't a visit-reader. Rank Trackers, Lookouts, Fortune Tellers, Cartographers, Scouts and Insomniacs as the visit threats, and the Oracle and Coroner as exact-role threats.
