entries.tip: The first time you're pressed for your night target, claim Ex-Con in one plain sentence. Say you visit a random player every night, aren't told whom, and read Evil to alignment checks. That explains a missing target, any Lookout or Tracker sighting of you at a victim, and a DIFFERENT Seer pair or Evil result. Ask for a Census Taker check: the census counts true alignment, so it is the one tool that clears you. Keep a will that maps where Cartographer, FT and Lookout data place your random visit each night, so sightings of you aren't misread. Evasive 'I can't name a target' answers build a case for your trial. The claim does name your exact role to a possible Ritualist, so don't volunteer it before you are pressed or read Evil; once you are, evasion costs more than the claim.

entries.tip: A player who publicly claims a role that exists only on the Yakuza side (Grunt, Clerk, Diviner, Pharmacist, Puppeteer, Ritualist, Smuggler, etc.) has given you the strongest lead you will get. This holds even if they label it '(Village)' and withdraw it as a typo once called out, and above all when an exact-role result (an archive, an Insomniac's visitor list, a profile, a survey) shows that role and nobody else claims it. Learn which faction every role belongs to, and check each claimed role, and each role any result shows, against that list the moment it is posted. Treat such a claim as a confession, not a wording slip, and hang that claimant the same Day, ahead of any vaguer case: left alive, they kill that night. Accurate results don't clear it. Evil investigators like the Diviner get true information, and a player confirming one of their hits (e.g. a Vigilante confirming the drawn role) authenticates that result, not the claimant. 'It was a slip, show me a mechanical result' must not shield them. Nominate and hang them while the Village still has the numbers, and if you said you lean Guilty, vote Guilty.

entries.tip: Report only what your role actually saw, and label everything else as a deduction from public claims (e.g. 'from Judy's and Frank's posts, X visited Y'). A Medic sees only her own protection, a Lookout only her target's visitors. A visit list your role can't produce costs you credibility for days, even when it's right. Village: ask once for the source of any full-night visit list before using it, and treat an unsourced one as the claimant's mistake to explain, not as evidence.

entries.tip: A nonzero token count on a player claiming a tokenless role (Vanilla, Grunt, Jester, Executioner, Serial Killer, Arsonist, Ex-Con) is a hard contradiction. A Philanthropist can't explain it: a gift to a role without tokens is thrown away and isn't counted. Only a token role can explain the count. Name the count, the claim it breaks and the roles it fits in one message before the vote.

entries.tip: When a strong suspect is nominated, even by someone you distrust or by a possible teammate, vote Yes if you hold any real lead (a self-incriminating slip, slot math, an Evil result). Passing a nomination only opens a trial, and you still decide at the trial. A No on a strong suspect's nomination wastes the chance, and while the Village still holds the numbers it hands the Yakuza a free night. Exception: if a Clerk may hold an unused rig, a passed nomination can mean an execution (see t38/t199).

Revealing your role costs far less than what the hang costs: the Jester's win, a revenge kill on a Guilty voter, and a second revenge kill if an Executioner targeting them also wins.

entries.tip: Count the full cost of a likely-Jester hang before voting. The revenge Divine-attacks a random Guilty voter the next night. entries.tip: Make vote pushes in public, not by private message. A PM asking for a Yes before a second source exists is visible to everyone as a trail, and opponents reframe it as a 'whip' to put you on trial. Post the evidence publicly and let the votes follow. Village: an honest player PMing for votes on a credible result (e.g. a Lookout log) is pushing clumsily, not proving a bloc. Judge the result they pushed, not the PMs.

entries.tip: Don't let an obvious Jester's self-nominations eat the Day. Sparing the Jester is not a reason to skip the day's hang: spend the Day's trials on the strongest Yakuza case (a count, a log, a refused night account). entries.tip: Under secret ballots, stated votes alone prove nothing: Evil players can announce Innocent and vote Guilty, or split their stated votes to look independent. At small counts, though, the totals can catch a misstated vote. If 3 of 4 voted Guilty and the nominee surely voted Innocent, everyone else who said Innocent lied, miscast or had their vote changed. Do this arithmetic after every small trial and publicly name whose stated vote the totals contradict, then ask that player to re-check their reminder and explain. An honest miscast or mispost is the commonest cause, and a player who corrects their own stated vote in public is more likely confused than Evil. Check for manipulation too. A Fixer flips one player's trial votes without telling them, and a Ballot Stuffer adds a vote (compare the total with the voter count). Nomination Yes counts can't be altered by either, so they are the cleaner check, and an Auditor sees the vote as counted. The mismatch is a lead, and the player becomes the next hang only when nothing mechanical points elsewhere. Never hang it ahead of a player with a mechanical killer case (an unexplained Katana survival, a first-person attack slip), look at which unconfirmed players are pushing that hang, and at 4-5 alive count what the hang leaves behind first (t206).

entries.tip: A profile lists three roles in alphabetical order: the target's true role, one role held by another player alive at the start of that night (never the Profiler's own), and one role that no player in the game has. You aren't told which is which. Before posting a profile, ask the target to state their exact role publicly, so they can't tailor a claim to the list. A list that omits their claimed role is a hard, hangable contradiction, unless it shows Roleplayer and they claimed a role a Roleplayer can be told. A profile also becomes an alignment read by elimination: if the target won't claim the list's Good role, or a trusted living claimant already holds it (it is then the likely 'other player' entry), every option left is Evil or Neutral. Roles can repeat, so that is strong odds, not proof: back it with a second source (a Seer pair, a cause of death, a vote record) and nominate. Once the target's role is settled, the other two entries split: one is a living player's role and the other is absent from the game. So a Yakuza-only leftover (Clerk, Wiretap, Pharmacist, Smuggler, Ritualist, Diviner, Ballot Stuffer) is a strong lead that the role is alive, not proof, and two Yakuza-only leftovers mean one of them is. A leftover Arsonist or Serial Killer is the same lead for a Neutral killer: say so aloud and start the hunt (t245) before the ignite. Match it to suspects and unclaimed players, e.g. a player who quoted a PM plus a Wiretap entry, and treat PMs as possibly read. If living players claim both leftover roles, one of those claims is almost surely false. Cross every profile with deaths, census results and confirmed claims to strike options. Post the full three-role list once it bears on a claim or a vote, and write it into your will as soon as you have it: a named Profiler is a sure guess for a possible Ritualist. Spend tokens on unclaimed players or on the contested side of a claim fight (e.g. two visitors to a Katana victim), whose role would decide a vote. Don't re-profile an active claimant to confirm them, since one profile never confirms a claim.

entries.tip: When a player quotes or closely paraphrases a private message they weren't party to, only an Eavesdropper (who visited the sender or receiver the night before) or the Yakuza Wiretap could have read it. Ask at once which role, and which player they eavesdropped. The named target must be in that exchange, and the visit must fit any Lookout, Tracker or visit-count data. A claim that can't name a fitting target, or a role list or profile decoy showing Wiretap, points to the Wiretap. Don't vote on the quoted PM's content until the quoter's access is explained.

entries.tip: You can't be role-blocked, and a Village blocker whose block on you fails is told it failed on immunity. Party Animals test claimed Vanillas this way. Don't hide behind Vanilla. Before Day 2, agree in night chat on a cover that explains immunity, 0 tokens and a visit each night. Party Animal fits all three, but only while no real Party Animal has claimed or posted blocks. Never name your real role, even loosely ('Pharmacist-type'). Each block you land is told to its target. If a claimed investigator posts a block notice and no Village blocker claims it, the block points at your team. So block a claimed Tracker only when the night's stakes justify it.

entries.tip: When roles stay hidden on death, use the night kill list as a claim test. A claimed investigator killed by the Katana was probably real, because the Yakuza kill the threats they can't explain away. In a duplicate or conflicting claim (e.g. a Sheriff calling a Seer Evil), the rival who survives deserves the test (audit, exact-role check, watch), and a fake read calling the Katana victim Evil collapses. A Katana death shows the victim wasn't Yakuza, not that they were Good: a Neutral can die to the Katana too, and it doesn't confirm every claim they made. Weigh it against the possibility that the Yakuza killed a real townie to leave a fake standing, and act on it before the next night rather than after. A Roleplayer is only ever told Sheriff, Tracker, Lookout, Seer, Fortune Teller, Oracle or Accountant, so a Katana-killed claimant of any other info role (Census Taker, Coroner, Bloodhound...) can't be an honest Roleplayer. Don't spend a Coroner token or a Day verifying them: act on their posted result at once.

entries.tip: Hunt Neutral killers on purpose; an unhunted Arsonist or Serial Killer often wins. Only killers that block wins matter here: a Bounty Hunter, Magpie, Jester or Executioner never blocks a Village win, and a Bounty Hunter who has spent its one token can't attack again. While the Katana still kills every night, never spend a Day's hang on a confessed or spent never-blocks-wins Neutral, and look hard at whoever rushes one to trial. Roles stay hidden on death, so the death announcements are your main evidence. Read every cause of death. An attack cause that isn't the Katana, a hanging, a Vigilante shot, a hidden gun (an Armed villager's one shot), a Veteran alert, a trap, a Bounty Hunter attack, a Jester or Executioner revenge, a curse (a Cursed player died) or Avenger (e.g. a Serial Killer attack or an Arsonist ignite) proves that killer is alive. A death by 'Avenger' means that player made a fatal attack on someone else who died that night, so check which cause killed the other victim. Two fatal causes on one victim mean two separate attackers. A multi-death night, or more deaths than the Katana, known shooters and trait effects (curse, Avenger) explain, points at an ignite. Quiet nights don't clear an Arsonist, who kills no one until it ignites. From Day 2 keep a written Neutral-killer suspect list: unclaimed or Vanilla claimants nobody has watched, players who survived an attack with no credible protector, players whose visits leave unexplained gaps in counts or groups, and anyone who admits an action but won't name it. Point Lookouts, Trackers, Oracle guesses (Arsonist, Serial Killer) and audits (0 tokens fits both) at them. A Not Evil Sheriff read doesn't clear them. The game can't end while one lives, and at two alive you can't hang them, so spend a hang on the best SK or Arsonist suspect well before the endgame, but never ahead of a stronger Yakuza case, and never on the Day before the Yakuza vote lock (t286): hanging a Neutral killer leaves the Yakuza count untouched, so at 5 alive with 2 Yakuza it hands them the game. The Yakuza want the rival killer hanged too, so check who nominates the Neutral suspect and who would supply the Guilty votes.

entries.tip: Nomination and trial ballots are secret, so the only record of how anyone voted is what they say, and nothing tracks it for you. Keep a notepad. For every nomination and trial, write each player's stated vote (Yes/No, Guilty/Innocent, or silent), the announced totals and your own vote. Mark when someone's stated vote later changes, contradicts their stated read, or doesn't fit the totals (e.g. more Guilty votes than players who said Guilty means someone hid a Guilty). A stated vote that doesn't fit a small trial's total is most often one miscast or misposted ballot: ask that player once to re-check their reminder, and never hang on the mismatch alone. Ask players to state their votes once, when a vote is actually coming, and quote the notepad when a claim shifts. A 'post stated votes' line tacked onto every message burns budget and is not a case.

entries.tip: You can't use tokens once you're dead: spend one-shot tokens (Clerk rig, Puppeteer, Ritualist, Medic tokens, swaps, ...) the first Day or night they can change a vote or remove a threat, rather than waiting for a perfect moment. A claimed or suspected player can die any night. Kill tokens (Vigilante, Sniper and Armed shots) are the exception to 'first chance': they need a lead first. Never fire one on Day 2 before any night result exists, and never at a bare claim clash. A second claimant of your own non-Unique role is often real, and twice now one real Sniper has killed the other. Once you have a lead, don't hold the shot for proof. At parity (the Yakuza hold half the votes) no nomination can pass, so fire it that Day even on a coin flip between two suspects. A puppet or doubled ballot lapses if you die the night you spend it (R21), and a Sniper's Day shot doesn't fire if you die before its random delay runs out (R25), so spend those ahead of a likely death. Yakuza: before spending a Day-effect token on a player (fix, puppet), check in night chat that your team isn't killing that player tonight.

entries.tip: (Team with a Smuggler) Don't veto the swap out of fear it will redirect your own attack. A swap moves exactly the actions aimed at the two swapped players, visiting or Astral, so plan it in night chat and know where the Katana goes. Use 1: beat the Medic. Aim the Katana at a decoy and swap the decoy with the player you really want dead, whom the Medic is likely protecting. The Katana lands on the real target, and the protection aimed at them moves to the decoy. Before submitting, work through both cases (the Medic guards the real target, the Medic guards the decoy). The kill only lands if the save isn't on the player the Katana ends up hitting. Use 2: dodge an investigation. If you expect to be checked tonight, swap yourself with a Villager. A Sheriff, Seer or audit aimed at you lands on them and reports their result under your name, and so do Astral checks: an Oracle guess, a Juror pair, a Scrutineer pick or a map. Your own team's actions move too: a Ritualist guess or Diviner pick aimed at a swapped player lands on the other, and a guess that misses that way outs the Ritualist and spends the tokens, so tell the team who is swapped. Random-draw effects (a Jester's or Executioner's revenge, a Cursed player's curse) are not moved. Never swap anyone with the Katana's target unless you mean to move the kill, and never swap yourself with the target. The Smuggler visits both swapped players, and both are told they were swapped. Expect them to post the notices, and have a cover ready for the visits.

entries.tip: Vote totals can be changed on purpose. A Ballot Stuffer's trial vote counts twice, so the total exceeds the voters. A Fixer secretly flips one player's Guilty/Innocent votes for a Day: the total stays the same, the player isn't told, and their reminder shows what they cast. So a trial total that contradicts honest stated votes may be a fix, not a lie. When a trial total doesn't fit, first ask every player who stated a vote to re-check their private reminder and repost it. A misposted public vote is the commonest cause, and a phantom-Fixer hunt can eat a whole Day. Only then list the fix and stuffer accounts before accusing. An Auditor (Village) and the Yakuza's Informant see fixed votes as counted. Neither role touches nomination (Yes/No) votes, so a Yes count that contradicts stated votes is the cleanest evidence of a hidden liar. A liar is not necessarily Yakuza, though. A nominee who votes Yes on their own nomination and then claims No is baiting the hang, which is a Jester tell (t91), not grounds to hang. Auditor: audit a player whose votes decided a close trial or who defended a suspect. Post night, target and the full record, and read a trial-vote mismatch as 'lied or fixed' but a Yes/No mismatch as a lie.

entries.tip: Examine bodies whose role would settle a live question: one side of a duplicate claim, a hanged suspect (did the hang hit a Yakuza?), a victim whose will may be forged, or a dead claimant whose results the town relies on but whose claim is disputed. A Katana victim is almost never Yakuza, so examining an undisputed Katana victim rarely settles anything; push for today's hang instead. Post night, target and exact role the next Day in one message, and keep the log in your will. Your exam is Astral, so no visit log can confirm it, and your report is your word until it fits other evidence. entries.tip: A Seer pair becomes a mechanical case only through an anchor. Once one member is independently confirmed Good (a Sheriff Not Evil plus an Oracle RIGHT, a self-proving action, a verified log), a DIFFERENT pair names the other as non-Good, so nominate them. After a hang, a Coroner exam confirming the hanged player's role extends the chain. A SAME pair between a confirmed Yakuza and another player points at that player too, unless the confirmed Yakuza held the Katana that night (then the partner read Good). Before the vote, say which anchor the chain rests on.

entries.tip: Before each night, count the likely Guilty votes on any trial that could hang a teammate. If fixing one pro-hang voter breaks the Guilty majority (a tie acquits), spend a token on that voter the night before. The trial on your own exposed teammate, or on yourself, is the trial that matters, so don't hoard tokens for a later one. Pick a voter who has said they will vote Guilty, since the fix flips the vote they actually cast. Offensively, at or near parity, fix a Villager likely to vote Innocent the night before the first close trial of a non-teammate. Their own Innocent then counts Guilty and can turn a narrow acquittal into a hang. The totals won't match that player's stated vote, so suspicion falls on them, not you. Agree in night chat that nobody fixes a player the Katana or Ritualist targets that same night: a dead voter casts nothing, and the token is wasted.

entries.tip: Post the exact visitor roles in your first message of the Day after they show something: a Yakuza-linked role, or a role that backs or breaks a key claim. entries.tip: Test a late Jester or Executioner claim on trial with mechanics, not the revenge threat. (1) Win check: Jesters and Executioners never block a win. If the game didn't end when the last known Yakuza died, some non-Village, non-Jester player is still alive. If the claimant is the only plausible one left, the Neutral claim fails. (2) Night pattern: a no-kill night on which only the claimant was blocked fits them holding the Katana. (3) Foreknowledge: did they name a role before its owner claimed it? That points to a Yakuza info role (Diviner, Wiretap), not an Executioner. (4) True-alignment counts: a census 'not Good' fits Neutral or Yakuza, so it decides nothing alone but combines with the above. If these converge, hang with a bare Guilty majority and keep confirmed info roles on Innocent.

entries.tip: Your count reads true alignment: the Katana holder's Good disguise, frames and Ex-Con readings don't fool it. Build a chain of cleared players. Ask every member of a group to confirm the count against what they know of themselves, so your claim becomes trusted. You pick only the first member; the other two are drawn at random from everyone else alive. Aim each census at one unknown: when both draws are already cleared, the count names that player exactly, and otherwise the group joins the chain for later subtraction. Post the group, the alignment counted and the count as soon as it bears on a vote or its members can confirm it. A Census Taker claim is a sure guess for a possible Ritualist (no Roleplayer is told it), so when one may be in the game write the full log in your will before you claim and expect to die that night. Neutrals are never counted, so phrase a gap as 'not Good' (Yakuza or Neutral), not 'Evil'. Keep the full log in your will.

entries.tip: Don't publicly raise deductions that corner your own team, such as claim-count or role-cap arguments that implicate teammates' claims. Let the town find them, or steer attention elsewhere. A Yakuza who 'helpfully' points out an overcount primes the case against their teammates.

entries.tip: If the game tells you a cap on how many players can hold a role (e.g. at most two Vanilla Villagers), count the claims against it from Day 2. More claimants than the cap allows means at least one is lying, a hard check that needs no reads. Press the latest and least-supported claimants first. A cap is not a role list, so without a stated cap fall back on t60's odds reasoning.

entries.tip: A claim already shown false stays false after the claimant 'corrects' it. 'Already corrected' is not an answer, and you don't need a new contradiction. Token claims are the cleanest test. A Magpie's victim is told which token kind was stolen, so a token count posted after a theft notice is a checkable false claim. An Accountant audit gives the true count. A Medic's Standard protection of another player is free, so '0 tokens' never explains a Medic protecting nobody while players die. Ask a token claimant once, plainly, whether they got a theft notice, and line their posted counts up against every audit and theft. If the story has changed to fit each new fact, hang them. Apply one standard to every nominee: don't acquit a broken claim and then hang someone else on lobbying alone.

entries.tip: Work from the roles that actually exist. If nobody claims a visit-tracking role (Tracker, Lookout, Fortune Teller) after the first request, stop asking for visit logs and work from votes, token audits and claims. Vote-reading roles (Juror, Scrutineer, Auditor) need trial data, so a Day 2 trial gives them something to read. But 'a trial for vote records' is a reason to open a trial, never to execute. Agree beforehand that it ends Innocent unless a corroborated case appears, and don't put one side of a live claim duel in the dock for it. Expect little from the records when the Yakuza vote with the majority and state their real votes. The ballots mostly pay off once you have a suspected pair to compare.

entries.tip: Read the Katana's victim list as 'who threatened the Yakuza', not 'who threatened today's suspect'. Keep a running list of each victim, whom they had last checked or challenged, what their next result could have shown about every living player (an audit reads any token-holder, a Bloodhound's trio count covers any attacker drawn into it), and who survives. When the Katana keeps killing whoever checked or pressed one quiet, uncontested claim, the player behind that claim and those who never challenged it are your leads. But when the victims were testers of a loud, already-disputed claimant who is left alive, don't conclude the kills protect him. Yakuza kill investigators for their own safety and leave a caught liar, often a Jester, standing as tomorrow's free mis-hang.

entries.tip: Steal only from players who claimed or are likely to hold tokens (Medic, Vigilante, Prosecutor, Surveyor, other token claims, and Yakuza fake-claiming one). Strike before they spend: a token used tonight can't be stolen. Stealing from Vanilla or tokenless claimants wastes the night. The victim is told which kind they lost, so your first theft also tests the target's claim (e.g. a Medic token proves a Medic-type count).

entries.tip: Pick pairs with several shared votes. Votes on the nomination or trial of either named player don't count, so a pair that includes the only nominee so far returns 'no shared votes': don't pair such a player until other trials exist. A pair with only one or two shared trials gives almost no signal, so wait until both have voted in a few trials. Aim at two suspects who seem to defend each other. A high match is a bloc lead, never a hang on its own. When a result shows something, post night, pair and exact counts, and keep every result in your will. If your result will look wrong against the public record, quote the exclusion rule in the same message, or the table will call it false. Juror isn't Unique: if another player claims it, both can be real, so compare results on a shared pair instead of duelling. A named Juror is a sure guess for a possible Ritualist (no Roleplayer is told it), so results that only confirm stated votes should stay in the will. entries.tip: Each night you learn three names and one combined count: every Attack those three have made this game, tonight's included. It never says which of the three attacked, and it is a running total, so early trios set the baseline. A 0 means none of the three has attacked yet (a role-blocked attack doesn't count, and a Yakuza who hasn't held the Katana also reads 0). A positive count gives a pool of three. Narrow it by crossing trios across nights with each other, with 0 trios and with confirmed players, and remember that Village attackers (Vigilante shots, Veteran alerts, trap hits) count too. Spend scent tokens to put a quiet player who claims no night action (a Vanilla, an Oracle with only 'wrong' guesses) from the pool your earlier draws left into the trio. entries.tip: Before every endgame hang and every night kill, count who will be alive at the next Day start and compare it with the Vulture threshold, max(floor(N/4),2), where N is the starting player count. That is 3 for 12-15 players and 2 for 11 or fewer. A living Vulture wins alone at a Day start with that many or fewer alive, and everyone else loses. A hang or kill that drops the count to the threshold therefore hands the game to any Vulture still alive. The Vulture is Unique and usually hides behind a quiet, no-action Vanilla claim, voting with the majority. Village: while an unverified quiet claimant lives, don't let a mis-hang bring the count to the threshold; spend the hang on the best killer case or on that claimant. Killers: if the threshold is near, remove the unverified quiet claimant rather than a confirmed villager. Add this check to the Jester and Executioner checks before any late hang.

entries.tip: Spend an early mark (Night 1-2) on one side of a contested claim, above all a duplicate investigator claim whose results conflict, or on an unclaimed suspect. If that player dies by any cause, their true role is announced, which settles the dispute, exposes a Roleplayer or fake claimant, and is one of the few ways a role becomes known now that deaths hide roles. Your mark is a visit, so when asked about your night action, say plainly at once whom you visited and on which night. Visitor logs will show the visit, and a 'no action' answer would contradict them. Calling it a mark names your exact role, a sure guess for a possible Ritualist. Your marks outlive you, so the claim costs you less than it costs most roles, but while one may be in the game and you still hold a token, add the Chronicler claim only when the visit needs explaining. Keep your marks in your will.

entries.tip: A Smuggler swap redirects every action aimed at either swapped player, whether or not it visits: the Katana, a Medic's save, a Sheriff check, a Seer pair, and Astral checks such as an Oracle guess, a Juror pair, a Scrutineer pick or a Cartographer's map. The result still names the player the user chose. Random-draw effects (a Jester's or Executioner's revenge, a Cursed player's curse) are not moved. Before hanging an investigator whose result looks impossible, or calling a survival or death story a lie, ask whether anyone posted a swap notice that night. Then recompute the result with the two players traded. A swap explains an odd result the way a role-block explains a missing one. Both swapped players are told, and Smuggler is a Yakuza role, so a swap notice proves a living Yakuza Smuggler. Post it the next Day.

entries.tip: Before calling anyone's vote-count claim false, agree which Day and which nomination or trial it refers to. entries.tip: Count down to the vote lock. A nomination needs a majority of living voters, so once the Yakuza hold half the living players they can block every nomination by voting No. With 1 Yakuza that happens at 2 alive (a nomination needs both votes), so at 4 alive a mis-hang plus the night kill leaves exactly that, and the hang at 4 alive is your last. With 2 Yakuza it happens at 4 alive (3 Yes needed); with 3 Yakuza, at 6. The Katana takes one Villager a night, a Ritualist can add up to two more over the game, and a Jester's revenge or a Cursed player's curse adds others. Katana and Ritualist victims are never Yakuza, so unless a hang was confirmed Evil, assume every Yakuza is still alive. With 3 Yakuza in 13, two mis-hangs can bring the lock by Day 4, so the Day 2 hang needs a corroborated fit, not a claim duel, and the Day 3 hang must go to a kill-faction candidate. The Day before the lock is your last real hang. Put your best suspect on trial that Day, even on a 50/50 group result such as a census that leaves two names, and prefer the defender of a hanged near-certain Yakuza to a disputed claim. A hang that removes a Neutral killer doesn't move the Yakuza count: at 5 alive with 2 possible Yakuza, hanging the Serial Killer leaves 2 of 4 and the night kill makes it 2 of 3. That Day's hang must go to your best Yakuza lead, even a weak one such as a PM pair, and before you cast a deciding Guilty, check whether the other Guilty votes come from that pair. Don't wait for a result that only arrives after the next night, because its holder is the likeliest kill. Post the count each morning: 'X alive, at most Y Yakuza, lock after Z more deaths.'

entries.tip: Ask every claimed Medic for each night's protection target the next morning, and line it up against the kill list. A real Medic usually covers the claimed info roles the Katana is likeliest to hit. A Medic whose protections keep landing on unattacked players while claimed investigators die unprotected is a strong Yakuza lead. A matching token count proves nothing, since a Ritualist also starts with 2 tokens. When a group result narrows a Yakuza to two names, look next at who shields the likelier one (urging 'don't pile on', voting with them): that player is the second-Yakuza lead. Turn it into a nomination, not just a remark.

entries.tip: A fake Medic claim gets checked against the kill list, because your team chooses the victim. If you claim Medic, report protections on plausible Katana targets: a claimed info role or the loudest Village voice. That night, have the Katana hit a different player, so the story reads 'my guard held, the Katana went elsewhere'. Never report protecting a player nobody would attack while claimed investigators die unguarded, and never report guarding the player who died. If you can't keep that up, pick a claim whose nightly output can't be checked but still fits your token count (see t4).

entries.tip: Keep a day-by-day log of every role claim, not just votes. A claim that gains a night, a token change or a new detail each Day (e.g. a Veteran's alerts going N1, then N1-N2, then N1-N3) reads as improvised, so quote the earlier wording and ask for the full history once. But piecemeal posting is also what an honest, disorganized claimant does, so treat drift as a lead to test, not a hang on its own. Claimants: state your complete history (every night, target, result, tokens spent) once, in one message, and repeat it word for word.

entries.tip: Choose the Katana holder from the team's cover claims, and agree the covers on Night 1 with the holder in mind. A Katana visit shows up in Fortune Teller counts, Cartographer groups and Lookout lists. The safest holder is a member whose real visiting action (Diviner, Fabricator, Pharmacist, Mortician) lands on the victim under a claimed visiting role, so the kill adds no extra visitor or group link. While an FT or Cartographer is active, never give the Katana to a member with no real visit (Wiretap, Grunt, Ballot Stuffer, Clerk, Informant) who claims Vanilla or another no-visit role. The first kill leaves one unexplained edge, and the late visiting claim needed to cover it, or a switch away from Vanilla, gets them hanged. If such a member must hold, give them a visiting claim from Day 2. Post the cover early on Day 2, before the counts are lined up. A claim that arrives last and exactly fills the graph's one gap reads as fitted. Check the cover against any archive or profile list before posting it.

support.note: Heidi (Ballot Stuffer) held the Katana N1 under a planned no-visit Insomniac cover. Carol's 6/6 and Dave's sizes left one edge, so she claimed Sheriff last and was hanged 11-1. Bob (Wiretap) claimed Vanilla, held N2, was mapped into the holder group and hanged after switching. Lessons from Heidi, Bob, Mallory, Niaj and the moderator.

entries.tip: Line up Fortune Teller counts, Cartographer sizes and every claimed visit. If the visitor count equals the number of claimed visitors (no spare slot), the Katana holder is hiding the attack behind one claimed visit. Usually it is a claimed visit that 'happened' to land on the victim (a check, a census, a watch), or a no-visit claimer linked into the victim's group. Say so outright: those claimants are the suspects. Allow for an Ex-Con's random visit as a floating edge. Split the suspects by claim order (a claim first posted after the numbers were public is the likeliest fit), by archive or profile lists, and by exact-role checks. Hang that Day rather than waiting a night.

support.note: Day 2: the 6/6 count, the 4,3,2,1,1,1,1 sizes and the posted targets left Erin (Lookout, claimed first) or Heidi (Sheriff 'check' on Katana victim Mallory, claimed last). Heidi was the holder. Reported by Alice, Carol, Dave, Erin, Ivan, Judy, Olivia.

entries.tip: Treat a role-claim switch made right after a map, count or census puts the player in a suspect group (e.g. 'I was Vanilla, actually I'm Medic') as a near-confession. It is exactly the cornered switch Yakuza are told to avoid. Spend that night's Oracle guess or profile on the new claim. A WRONG plus the switch is enough to hang. 'I hid as Vanilla on Day 2 to stay safe, as the tips say' doesn't excuse it.

entries.tip: Use a public archive list as a tiebreak once the evidence has narrowed to two rival claims. A real holder's role appears only if that player was sampled, and a fake appears only by chance among all roles. So a claimed role on the list is several times likelier to be real than one missing from it (roughly 5-10x in a 13-player game). That is enough to break a 50/50 the visit math already produced when a night's delay costs a kill. It is not a standalone case. A listed role is also a ready-made fake claim for the Yakuza, so a new claim of a listed role still needs a test.

support.note: Lookout (Erin) was listed and Sheriff (Heidi) wasn't. Judy and Ivan used the list to break the Erin/Heidi tie, and Heidi was the holder.

entries.tip: When a teammate has to make a fresh or changed claim, assume a living Oracle (or Profiler) will test that exact role that night. Kill the likeliest tester that night instead of a lower-value target, or the next Day's WRONG hangs the teammate.

support.note: Bob: his switched Medic claim was Oracle-guessed WRONG the same night, while the Katana killed someone else.

Carol, Dave, Alice: Carol's Party Animal cover collided with real PA Judy, the living Oracle guessed that exact role on N3 and the WRONG broke it. The Oracle was never the Katana target until N5, when the holder was blocked.

entries.tip: An uncontested Sheriff's posted results are the Village's best information, so don't discount them because no second source exists yet. Asking for a second check is fine when two investigators exist, but demanding one that can't come only stalls. An Evil read on an unverifiable claim is a mechanical case on its own (t38). When a credible Sheriff is alive, steer their checks to the unchecked players and spend hangs on unchecked suspects before anyone their reads have touched.

support.note: Dave (0.16) filed 'hurt' on a 'demand a second check' line: Grace's genuine reads were discounted, the town hanged Not Evil Erin, and the Sheriff died N4 with her clears unused. Alice (0.16) argued for second checks, Frank found them useful early. Thin, mixed evidence.

entries.tip: A result from one unverified claimant that was held back and then names the very player who just accused them is retrofitted until tested, so don't hang on it. 'He posted his count before any visitor spoke' is not evidence either: a Jester or Yakuza can post a fake first and call every contradicting visitor a Roleplayer. When two independent claims confirm each other (e.g. an audit of 0 tokens matching a Lookout claim) against one lone counter, the story that needs two Roleplayers is the weaker one. If the accused offers a cheap overnight test of the counter's claim (a scent, an audit, a secret gift or visit the counter must report), vote Innocent and run it. A claimant who waves off a test of their own result is the likelier liar, possibly a Jester: test or ignore them rather than hang their target.

support.note: Moderator plus Carol, Dave, Erin, Grace, Heidi, Ivan, Mallory, Niaj, Olivia, Alice, Bob, Judy: Jester Bob's fake one-visit count and held-back 'map' named Lookout Heidi right after she named him. Heidi and Accountant Grace contradicted him and offered Dave's scent and Mallory's gift as tests. The Village hanged Heidi 9-3 on 'he claimed first', and that mis-hang decided the game.

entries.tip: An Oracle claim whose log holds only 'wrong' guesses is uncheckable and is the natural Ritualist cover: both guess roles astrally, with no visits. Treat it as unverified, more so once a Ritualist kill has appeared, when its guesses land on night victims, when its owner dodges a Jester revenge pool, or when its first decisive 'WRONG' appears just as it is needed against a rival of another claimant. Test it early, while the Village still has the votes: an audit (a Ritualist starts with 2 tokens, an Oracle has 0), a scent, or a hang ahead of roles that can't be faked.

support.note: Carol, Erin, Mallory, Grace, moderator: Judy (Ritualist) claimed Oracle with three 'wrong' guesses, was never nominated before D4, and used a fake WRONG to help hang real Scrutineer Ivan.

entries.tip: A loud duel between two info claimants can have no Yakuza on either side, since the liar may be a Jester or a Roleplayer. The real Yakuza then coast beside it in claims nobody can check: a Vanilla, an all-'wrong' Oracle, a duplicated role, each voting with every majority and stating their votes truthfully. While the duel runs, point audits, scents and questions at those coasters. After one mis-hang, turn the next trial to them, not to the duel's other side, and check who quietly rode the majority.

support.note: Moderator, Dave, Erin, Grace, Mallory: Alice (Vanilla), Judy (all-wrong Oracle) and Frank (second Scrutineer) were never nominated before D4 while the Village spent both real hangs on the Bob/Heidi fight. All three Yakuza voted Yes and Guilty with the crowd; the three Innocent voters on Heidi were all Village.

entries.tip: Vote-reading claims (Scrutineer, Juror, Auditor) are trivial to fake: a fake result only has to match the stated votes and totals, and disciplined Yakuza state their real votes. But only Unique roles (Smuggler, Vulture) are limited to one copy, so two claimants of one of these roles can both be real. A duplicate is a reason to test both, never proof that one lies, and 'only one can be real' is not a case. If a second player claims your role, test them that Day, and don't assume the later claimant is the copier. Ask each claimant for something only the real role sees, such as the exact wording and name order of the private result line, and get the rival's answer before the real holder posts theirs. On Day 2 these roles have no result yet (no trial has happened), so don't spend the Day demanding one or put a claimant on trial for lacking it; move to other leads. Later, compare the two claimants' results on a shared pair and against the record, applying the role's exclusions first (t305). Real holders: check the rival and suspected teammate pairs, not players whose votes nobody doubts.

entries.tip: A fake vote-reading claim (Scrutineer, Juror) needs no visits and is hard to break. Build each fake result only from publicly stated votes that fit the announced totals. Avoid draws that include teammates, the nominee or disputed voters. Learn the role's exact result wording and format first (e.g. Scrutineer names come alphabetically), because a real holder can quiz you. Claim it before the real holder speaks, so they look like the copier. It audits as 0 tokens, so if you hold tokens, remove any Accountant early. Tell your team before you change an agreed claim.

support.note: Alice, Frank, Judy, moderator: Frank's fake Scrutineer results used only stated votes, Ivan could not contradict them, and the real Scrutineer was hanged as the copier. Frank switched from the agreed Vanilla without telling the team; the Katana had removed Accountant Grace on N2.

entries.tip: You know your team's own visits, so a town player whose 'result' names someone else as the Katana visitor is a proven liar: a Jester or other Neutral, not a Villager. Don't expose them. Back them mildly, let the Village hang their target, and leave them alive as the next Day's hang. Spend the night kills on the investigators who can read your team (audits, attack counts, vote checks). At the liar's trial keep one teammate on a stated Innocent citing Jester risk: that member stays out of the revenge pool and gains credit when the Jester win is announced.

support.note: Alice, Frank, Judy, moderator: Bob's fake map named Heidi for Alice's own Katana visit, so the team read him as a Jester, let Heidi hang, killed Grace and Dave, left Bob as the D3 hang, and Judy voted Innocent. Two Village hangs were wasted at no Yakuza risk.

Moderator, Grace, Frank: the team let Jester Bob take the D3 hang and the Village Sniper duel do its own damage. Both Yakuza voted Guilty in the 6-0, so the revenge could have hit them (2 of 5); it took Medic Alice.

entries.tip: Count toward parity in night chat and stack every extra kill source on the night before it: the Katana, a Ritualist guess on a firm claim, a swap to get past a possible Medic, and a ballot token for the next Day. Several deaths in one night can take you from a minority to vote control before the town can regroup. Script the next Day for each possible count (who posts, who nominates, how each votes).

support.note: Judy, Frank, Alice: on N3 the Katana (via swap), the ritual and a ballot token were all spent together. With the Jester revenge and Cardinal curse, 9 alive became 4 with 3 Yakuza, and Ivan was hanged 4-1 on D4.

entries.tip: Oracle is a workable cover: the guess is Astral, there are no visits, and 'wrong' results need no proof. Sharp villagers know it is the obvious Ritualist cover, so keep the fake log on living, uncontroversial players and never on Katana victims. Save one fake 'guessed X = their claimed role, WRONG' for the endgame, to sink a real villager who shares a role claim with a teammate. An audit shows your unspent ritual tokens against an Oracle's 0.

support.note: Judy, Niaj, Alice: Judy's Oracle claim with three 'wrong' guesses was never broken, and her late WRONG on Ivan's Scrutineer claim carried the final hang. Carol and Mallory flagged it as the natural Ritualist cover, but too late.

entries.tip: If you hold a role a Roleplayer can be told (Sheriff, Tracker, Lookout, Seer, Fortune Teller, Oracle, Accountant), don't volunteer 'unless I'm a Roleplayer' when your result contradicts a claim nobody has confirmed. It hands the accuser a ready way to dismiss you. State your result flatly and show that the rival's specific claim is false under every reading. Flag yourself as a possible Roleplayer only when a confirmed result contradicts you (t99).

support.note: Heidi: her own Roleplayer caveat in her claim and will gave Bob and the voters the 'both visitors are Roleplayers' excuse. Single report.

entries.tip: Before calling a posted result 'provably false', recompute it yourself from the role's text, exclusions included. A Juror's counts leave out every vote on the nomination or trial of either named player, so 'no shared votes yet' is correct when the only trials so far were of one of the pair. Scrutineer and Census Taker groups add random players, and a Seer pair compares appearances. A result that seems to conflict with the public record is a question for the claimant ('which rule gives that?'), not proof of a lie. One conflicting line is never enough to hang or prosecute on, least of all at 4-5 alive. Claimants: when your result will look odd against the record, quote the rule that explains it in the same message.

support.note: Moderator (0.4), Grace, Bob, Dave, Frank (0.16 each): Dave's honest N2 Juror result 'Frank and Alice: no shared votes yet' was right, since the only trial was Frank's and the Juror excludes it. Grace, Bob and Carol called it provably false, Bob prosecuted Dave, and the real Juror was hanged D4 at 4 alive, which lost the game.

Moderator, Bob: Alice called Bob's N1 trap on Erin 'impossible' and Bob himself described it as 'placed after she died'. Both were wrong on the rules (night actions resolve together), and the false 'contradiction' fed the release on Bob.

entries.tip: An Insomniac's list shows the true role of up to three of the night's visitors, whatever they claim, and the Katana visit shows its holder's real role. Every Yakuza role name is Yakuza-only, so one listed visit proves your team is visiting. While a claimed Insomniac still holds tokens (2 at the start), make them the Katana target: a result from the night they die is never posted. If you can't, visit as little as possible on nights they may stay awake (the holder only, with no extra role action), and treat any result announced for tonight (Insomniac, map, track) as certain to happen. Never claim a role the list has shown. It gives roles, not names, so stay on a Village cover.

support.note: Moderator, Dave, Carol: Bob said on D2 he would spend his last Insomniac token on N2. Dave, the last Yakuza, still killed Tracker Frank and also divined Bob, the list read 'Diviner, Tracker' again, and he was hanged D3. Killing Bob instead would have buried the result. One game.

entries.tip: If the game's setup tells you which roles are never in play (e.g. 'no Vanilla Villager, no Grunt'), check every role claim against that list the Day it is made. A claim of an excluded role is impossible: call it out at once and ask for a real role. It is a lie, not a faction read. Paired with a thin push, a self-nomination or 'hang me', it fits a Jester (t91), so don't spend more Guilty votes on it than a bare majority. Yakuza and Neutrals: never use an excluded role as cover. If the usual Vanilla cover is ruled out, say 'no night action' and name a role only when pressed, picking one the setup allows.

support.note: Moderator (0.4), Carol, Mallory, Olivia, Alice (0.16 each): this setup excluded Vanilla Villager and Grunt. Jester Mallory claimed Vanilla on D2, Ivan caught it the next morning, and the claim plus 'hang me' drew 8 Guilty. One game.

entries.tip: A dead investigator's posted results are one claimant's word until something confirms the role. A Coroner exam showing the claimed role does that, and it also rules out a Roleplayer, who shows as 'Roleplayer'. Ask the Coroner for that exam before the town hangs on a dead Seer's, Tracker's or Sheriff's result. A confirmed role confirms that the result was real, not what you inferred from it: re-read it with the role's limits (a Seer pair compares appearances; the holder reads Good, an Ex-Con or framed player reads Evil) and add a second pointer, such as a profile, a cause of death or a vote record, before the vote.

support.note: Moderator (0.4), Grace, Carol, Niaj, Heidi (0.16 each): Carol's exam showed Frank was a real Seer, so his Erin/Carol pair plus Ivan's profile hanged the SK 6-3. Niaj, Heidi and Erin note that the exam proves the role, not the reading of the pair.

entries.tip: You see every trial ballot. In night chat, report who voted Innocent on your exposed teammates and who led the Guilty side, and use that to choose Katana targets and to spot hidden investigators. Never show vote knowledge in public that secret ballots hide. Your own ballot is as readable as anyone's: once a teammate is doomed, vote Guilty and say so (t16). An Innocent on a hopeless trial plus a public defense marks you for the Vigilante.

support.note: Judy (0.16) and the moderator's review: Informant Judy defended Heidi and voted Innocent in the 5-2 hang, and Olivia shot her that night. Thin: the vote readings never visibly steered a kill.

entries.tip: Spend Katana kills on Village players who can vote you out. A Bounty Hunter, Jester, Executioner or Magpie never blocks your win and often votes with you, so killing one wastes the night. Before each kill, above all as the last Yakuza, count the next Day's votes: pick the victim whose death leaves the Village short of a nomination and Guilty majority (e.g. you plus a Neutral against two Villagers is 2-2, and no hang passes). Don't openly back a Jester's self-nominations either: the town suspects whoever pushes that hang.

support.note: Moderator: lone Yakuza Ivan killed Bounty Hunter Heidi on N3, who had voted with him. That left Alice, Erin and Frank, who hanged him 3-2 on D4. Killing Alice or Frank would have left a 2-2 split with Jester Dave. One game.

entries.tip: When a player keeps self-nominating or begging for the rope, refuse the hang (t91) and note who keeps voting Yes or Guilty on them and trading PMs with them. Yakuza and other non-Village players gain from a wasted hang and a revenge on a Guilty voter. It is a lead, not a verdict: ask that backer for a role claim and a public summary of their PMs, and treat a refusal as the case.

support.note: Moderator: Ivan (Wiretap) voted Yes and Guilty on Jester Dave's self-nominations and had a PM cluster with Dave and Heidi. The Village turned on him, he dodged the PM content and any role claim, and he was hanged as the last Yakuza. Heidi, a Bounty Hunter, backed the push too, so the pattern also catches Neutrals. One game.

entries.tip: Check a Veteran claim against the announced causes of death, which are public even though roles are hidden. A death whose cause is a Veteran's alert proves a Veteran was on alert that night and that the dead player visited them, so a claimant who named that night and victim is corroborated without any second source. Don't spend Days asking for more proof. Use it: a visitor killed by an alert on a night with no Katana death was probably the Katana holder unless a Village visit explains it (a Medic, a watcher), so look at the dead visitor's claims and links for teammates.

support.note: Carol, Erin (0.16 each): Erin's alert account matched every death (Carol N1 with no Katana kill, Bob N2), yet the table argued for three Days over a dead Fortune Teller's count instead of treating the claim as checked. Alice, Frank, Heidi and Dave called it unverifiable; the death causes were the check. Thin: one game.

entries.tip: Shoot on a mechanical lead, never on a claim clash, and never on Day 2 before any night result exists. Sniper isn't Unique, so a second Sniper claimant may be real; twice now two real Snipers have shot at each other and the Village lost one. Ask them for their token count, test them with a vote or a Sheriff check, and shoot only if another result breaks their claim. Never shoot a player with a corroborated Not Evil read. Good leads: an Evil read the claim doesn't explain, a broken or copied claim, the PM partner of a player a death cause showed to be an attacker, the players who nominated and stated Guilty against a corroborated clear, or one of the last two names an elimination leaves once tracks, blocks on the kill night and proven roles have struck the rest. Nobody is told who shot, so don't announce a shot: a declared shot invites one back. Your shot fires after a random delay of up to n-1 speaking turns and not at all if you die first (R25), so a shot fired back at someone who already shot at you often loses the race. Night protection is gone by Day but innate Defense is not: a Basic shot fails on a Jester or Executioner, and only Strong beats a Serial Killer or Arsonist. The outcome of a Day shot is announced to everyone, so a 1-token shot that a suspect survives shows innate Defense to the whole table: a cheap public test of a Neutral-killer suspect you can't kill, with the hang to follow. Don't hold your last token for proof: fire it at your best unchecked suspect before the Yakuza can hold half the votes. If they already hold half (e.g. 2 v 2), they vote down every nomination and the next night kill ends the game, so shoot that Day even on a coin flip between two suspects: a hit gives the Village back its hanging majority. Or use the token as the innate-Defense test once only a Neutral killer is left.

entries.tip: Once a Not Evil read is corroborated (e.g. a Tracker saw the Sheriff visit that player), the players who nominate that player or say they vote Guilty against the read are your best leads. Sheriff: check them next and never spend a night re-checking a player you already cleared. Shooters: aim there. Everyone: ask each pusher for a role claim and a mechanical reason. The holder caveat (t31) still applies to the cleared player, but not to the question of who is pushing.

support.note: Moderator (0.4), Alice, Dave (0.16 each): Frank nominated Dave on D2 and Frank and Grace stated Guilty against Carol's Not Evil read, which Erin's track corroborated. Carol checked Bob, then Dave again on N3, and never checked Frank or Grace, the two Yakuza, who voted identically all game.

entries.tip: If a result (a profile, a survey, a count) corners a teammate into claiming the same role as a live Village claimant, don't Katana that claimant the next night. Killing the one player who contradicts the copy tells the town who the copier is, and if the victim is an Avenger the holder dies and is named as the attacker as well. Kill someone else, such as the investigator whose result boxed your teammate in, and let the duel stand unresolved. Never post the rival's numbers word for word as your own. Better still, agree covers on Night 1 so nobody has to improvise a copy (t61).

support.note: Moderator (0.4), Bob (0.16): Bob copied Alice's N1 Cartographer sizes, the Yakuza killed Alice on N2, her Avenger trait killed holder Carol, and on D3 every Villager named Bob as the copier. Ivan shot him that turn. One game.

entries.tip: (If you have the Armed trait) Your hidden gun is one Basic shot at night, and it is a visit. Fire it at your best Yakuza lead (a claim broken by a profile or count, the PM partner of a player shown to be an attacker) while a Yakuza is still alive: a gun you never fire is worth nothing. Basic can't kill a Serial Killer or Arsonist (Standard Defense) or a Jester, Executioner or Magpie (Basic Defense), so once only a Neutral killer is left the gun won't finish them and the hang is the kill. A shot that fails on a suspect no Medic guards is evidence of innate Defense, so post it the next Day. A wrong shot costs more if the victim is Cursed or an Avenger.

support.note: Moderator (0.4), Grace, Dave (0.16 each): Erin and Grace each held an Armed shot all game. Neither fired at Bob or Carol while they lived, and against Arsonist Heidi's Standard Defense the shots could no longer kill. One game.

entries.tip: When no result is coming (the Katana has stopped because the Yakuza look dead, no living role can read a Neutral killer, and the R14 stall clock is running), 'I'll only vote on hard results' is a stall, not a standard. Rank the living players by what each has made checkable: an exact role, a target for every night, and results that deaths, an archive or a profile have since confirmed. Ask each for that log by name, once. The player who gives none of it, answers with filler and names targets only once on trial is the best case you will get: nominate them while enough Villagers are alive to convict. A confirmed role's clumsy wording about one night is not a case, and a trial on it wastes the Day.

support.note: Moderator (0.4), Alice, Ivan (0.16 each): Days 4-5 went on 'only hard results' and a 0-6 trial of Auditor Frank over wording while Arsonist Heidi gave no role or targets and then ignited two players. Both correct kills (Bob, Heidi) came from a copied claim, a PM trail and evasion. One game.

Moderator (0.4), Alice (0.16): with the Sheriff dead after N2 no result was coming, yet the table kept repeating 'only checkable info' and nominated nobody until D3. The Yakuza pair's vague PM answers and no-action claims were the best case available and went unused.
Frank: no investigator was alive after N1, yet the table waited on results through D2. The PM pair and the claimless Heidi were the best cases available and neither was nominated.

entries.tip: You read only the votes your target cast on the Day just before the night. A Day with no nomination gives you nothing, and so does auditing a quiet player who cast no vote. Audit someone who voted in that Day's nomination or trial and whose vote matters: the deciding vote, a suspect's defender, a stated vote the totals don't fit. Report each night once, in fixed words ('N3: no audit', or 'N2: audited X, Yes on Y's nomination, Innocent at the trial'), and never call a result 'pending'.

support.note: Frank: his audit of Bob returned 'no votes', and his three wordings for an empty Night 3 got him nominated on D4 (acquitted 0-6). One low-weight report.

entries.tip: Post an Evil read as what it is: 'X reads Evil, which fits a Yakuza, a Jester, an Executioner, an Ex-Con or a framed player'. Never post it as 'X is Yakuza'. Before pushing a hang on it, check the target's record: a self-nomination on any Day, a hang pushed with no data or a weak defense points at a Jester, and then your read is a reason to leave them alive and check someone else. If the town hangs them anyway, vote Innocent yourself and say why: the revenge draws from the Guilty voters, and you are the investigator it would cost.

support.note: Moderator (0.4), Alice, Dave, Frank, Grace (0.16 each): Alice declared Erin 'Yakuza' on her N2 Evil read though Erin had self-nominated on D2. All 7 voted Guilty, the Jester won, and the revenge drew Alice herself (she also died to the Katana that night). One game.

entries.tip: Charm the player likeliest to be attacked tonight (a claimed investigator, a player the killers just failed on), not an arbitrary one. Never announce a charm, a held attack or a release target, however hard the table presses: the players demanding it are often the killers, and a named Kitsune holding a kill is the night's first target. While you hold a swallowed attack you can't charm anyone, yourself included, and it is lost if you die. So release it within a night or two, but on a real lead: an unexplained Katana survivor, a claimless or late-Vanilla player once a killer's cause of death has shown, a PM pair who push the same line. Never release on a claim clash. Only Smuggler and Vulture are Unique, so a second claimant of any role, Kitsune included, may be real, and a release on a rival claimant has twice killed a Villager. Use the level you were told. A swallowed Strong attack (a Serial Killer's) is one of the few night kills that beats an Arsonist's or Serial Killer's Standard Defense; a swallowed Katana is only Standard and fails there. The cause you swallowed proves that killer is alive and that your ward is not that killer: post it when it bears on a vote, weighing that an exact Kitsune claim feeds a possible Ritualist. Check whether the ward reported two attacks, which fits two charms. If another Kitsune exists, split your wards: two charms on one player leave both of you holding attacks and nobody able to protect the next night. A release is announced with the swallowed attack's cause, so say afterwards that the death was yours.

While you hold a swallowed attack you can't charm anyone, so release it within a night or two on your best-supported killer suspect: it is lost if you die. Use the level you were told. entries.tip: A Kitsune changes how deaths and survivals read. A kill released by a Kitsune is announced with the cause of the attack it swallowed, so a later 'Serial Killer' or 'Katana' death may be a release and not a fresh attack: ask every claimed Kitsune what they hold and whom they released on before counting killers. Test a Kitsune claim against the ward's own notices: a charmed player is still told the role behind each attack they survived, so the claimed level and cause must match what the ward reports. Two attack notices on one ward fit two real Kitsunes. A Kitsune holding an attack can't protect, so ask where the held attack is going before the night.

support.note: Grace, Erin, Bob (0.16 each) and the moderator's review: Carol's N2 notice of a Katana and an SK attack matched both Kitsune stories, yet the table treated one claim as fake. Erin's N3 'Serial Killer' death was Heidi's release, not Dave's attack. One game.

entries.tip: Count the Days you have left on Day 2. Two different kill causes on one night (a Katana death plus a Serial Killer death) mean the town loses up to two players every night. At 6 alive that leaves at most two hangs, so a Day with no nomination loses the game and 'wait for tonight's results' is not an option. Ask each claimant once for night, target and exact result, set a round by which someone nominates, and put the best case available on trial: one side of a duplicate investigator claim, a late Vanilla claimant, an unexplained survivor.

entries.tip: Your free attack is Basic and can't kill a Serial Killer or Arsonist (Standard Defense), so against a Neutral-killer suspect pay 1 token for Strong. Visit the player likeliest to attack tonight: a late Vanilla claimant read Not Evil once a Serial Killer cause of death has appeared, or the likely Katana holder (Basic is enough for a Yakuza). Blind free visits on Nights 1-2 rarely fire. Pay for the two-target visit once the holder is narrowed to two suspicious claimants, above all on a night the Katana is likely to move: it tends to pass to whoever the Sheriff is about to check or to a suspected fake claimant, because the holder reads clean. A kill there proves the dead player attacked. A blocked player makes no attack, so a Village blocker on the same suspect cancels your visit: agree in public that blocker and Enforcer cover different suspects. Your attack lands only if they attack that night, and it doesn't cancel theirs: if you are their target you both die. Don't describe a result in your role's own terms while unclaimed ('visited X, X made no attack' names you an Enforcer and draws a block or the Katana): give no result or a full claim. Claiming Enforcer and pressing a suspect in public can draw their attack onto you, which makes the trade likely, so make it only when removing the killer is worth your role. Dying with all three tokens is the usual waste.

entries.tip: An Enforcer's attack lands only on a player who attacks that night, and a Strong one (1 token) beats your Standard Defense. When a claimed Enforcer is alive and questioning you, skip your kill that night: if you don't attack, their visit does nothing. Attacking the Enforcer on a night they visit you kills you both, which is a loss for a role that must be the last one alive. Let the Katana and the hangs thin the table, and kill again once the Enforcer is dead or busy elsewhere.

support.note: Moderator (0.4), Grace (0.16): on D3 claimed Enforcer Alice asked Grace about her N2 action. Grace attacked Alice on N3 anyway, Alice's Strong visit killed her, and the last Yakuza won. Holding the kill would have put Grace on D4 alive with Alice and Carol. One game.

entries.tip: Don't nominate the player who counterclaimed your fake claim, or the player who just survived your Katana, unless you have counted a Yes majority and can cite a result. A failed nomination of the Katana survivor marks the nominator as the attacker's side and invites an immediate counter-nomination that passes. Let a Villager open the push and add your Yes late, or keep the pressure verbal until you have a result to stand on.

support.note: Moderator (0.4), Bob, Carol, Alice, Erin (0.16 each): on D3 fake Sheriff Bob nominated real Sheriff Heidi, who had survived the N2 Katana. It failed with 2 Yes, Grace nominated Bob minutes later citing the push and his PM, and he was hanged 3-2. One game.

entries.tip: In a duplicate investigator claim, see which claimant the Katana goes after. A claimant who reports a Katana attack the morning after, with a Medic stating a protect on them that night, is very likely the real one: Yakuza don't spend the Katana on their own fake. The rival who then nominates the survivor with no new result is your best hang that Day. Check the Neutral case too: an innate-Defense survivor has no protector to name (t43).

support.note: Heidi, Erin, Frank (0.16 each): Heidi posted her N2 Katana survival at dawn, and Erin's protect on her matched. Fake Sheriff Bob then nominated Heidi with no result. He was Yakuza and was hanged, though on the PM and the push more than on this reading. One low-weight game.

entries.tip: Treat repeated public demands to name tonight's target, your stored attack or your trap's location as a warning sign, not a duty. The players who gain most from the answer are the killers, and they will ask in the Village's voice ('just so we can check it'). Refuse once in one calm line ('it goes up after the night resolves') and note who keeps pressing: that is a lead to question, not proof. Claim a power role only when the claim settles a vote that Day.

support.note: Moderator: Carol and Dave (Yakuza) and Heidi (SK) all pressed Kitsune Grace on D2 to name her release target. She claimed and named Bob, and both killers hit her that night. One game.

entries.tip: Once the Village is a minority beside two hostile sides (e.g. 2 Villagers, 2 Yakuza and a Serial Killer at 5 alive), no hang passes on Village votes alone, and the two killing sides will otherwise agree on a Villager. Each wants the other gone, so pitch a hang to whichever side gives you the third vote, and name both leads aloud (the PM pair, the late-Vanilla killer suspect). Count what each hang leaves before choosing. Hanging a Yakuza with the Neutral killer's vote leaves no side holding half. Hanging the Neutral killer with Yakuza votes leaves 2 Yakuza of 4, which is lost unless an armed trap or a kill token can still hit the holder that night. Never spend that Day defending one Villager against another.

support.note: Moderator: on D3 Alice and Frank faced Carol, Dave and Heidi. Nobody pushed Heidi or the pair, and the three hostile votes hanged Alice 3-2. The moderator's version is 'push the late Vanilla; the Yakuza may help'. The what-it-leaves count is added by arithmetic, not from play. One game, thin.

entries.tip: An unclaimed player whose result reads like 'visited X, X made no attack' is an Enforcer. Its attack lands on whoever attacks that night; even the free Basic one kills a Katana holder with no Defense, and a paid double visit covers two suspects at once. While it lives, block it every night or kill it. Keep the Katana on the member it is least likely to visit: never the teammate the table already suspects, and never one who publicly blocked it. Don't post that you blocked it, since that tells it whom to visit next. A Diviner's Strong Defense on the holder stops even a Strong Enforcer attack.

entries.tip: A death whose cause is an Enforcer's attack proves the dead player made an attack of their own that night. If a Katana death happened the same night, they were very likely the holder, and a Not Evil Sheriff read on them that night is expected, not a clear. Treat their role claim as broken, then look at whose results propped that claim up and who defended it.

entries.tip: Holding back your exact role doesn't hide you if you post a result in your role's own words. 'My read is consistent with her Vanilla claim' names a Sheriff, and 'I visited X and X made no attack' names an Enforcer: the Yakuza read the wording and block or kill you that night. While unclaimed, either post no result at all or make the full claim when the result bears on a vote. The half-post is the worst of both.

support.note: Frank and Bob (1.0 each), confirmed by the moderator: Frank's 'consistent with her Vanilla claim' drew the N2 Katana (saved only by a Kitsune charm), and Bob's 'made no attack' wording got him blocked on N2. entries.tip: Protectors and other roles with no results to post: don't press everyone else to claim while holding back even your own role type. Once the table starts eliminating candidates for a hidden killer, the last unexplained player is the default hang. Give your category by Day 2-3 ('protective, no results') and the exact role with your night log as soon as the elimination reaches you. On trial, never name as a suspect a player your own log shows you trusted, such as one you just spent a token protecting: the table reads it as a contradiction. Name the other remaining candidate with the mechanical case against them, and offer a cheap check of your own claim (an Oracle guess tonight).

entries.tip: Narrow a Serial Killer by who could not have made each kill. A player confirmed role-blocked on a night a Serial Killer death still happened can't be that killer. Build this list from Day 3, strike the confirmed players and name the candidates left; then aim an Oracle guess of 'Serial Killer' or a blocker at the likeliest one. Count a block confirmation only when blocker and blocked player are independent: a Yakuza pair can confirm each other's fake block and 'visited no one' track. A Katana survival does not strike anyone, since a Serial Killer's Standard Defense stops the Katana.

entries.tip: When the table says aloud whom you should check tonight, the Yakuza can hand that player the Katana so they read Not Evil. Check someone nobody suggested, and note who asked for a check on a player who then came back clean. Use your checks while several Yakuza are alive: you can never find a Serial Killer (it reads Not Evil), and once one Yakuza is left the holder reads clean every night, so late checks are nearly worthless. From then on work from who could not have made each kill and from exact-role results.

entries.tip: Spend Counts on a question that decides a live dispute or a team decision: count a role two players both claim to learn whether one is fake, count Sheriff or Seer to tell your Fabricator whether frames matter, count Enforcer or Party Animal before moving the Katana onto a suspected teammate. Don't spend one on what you can already infer (a Serial Killer cause of death already proves a Serial Killer). You get one token a night and three in all, so a wasted Count is missing in the endgame, when one exact-role fact can decide a vote.
